definition_zh: 股东；持有公司股份的人或机构
definition_en: a person or organization that owns shares in a company
core_image: 公司被切成许多等份，一只手握住其中一份并举起表决卡
scene: 年度股东大会开始前，一位持有公司股份的人翻看表决材料，抬头询问董事会为何没有派发利润。The shareholder asked the board why profits were not paid out.
sceneCN: 这里指「持有公司股份的人或机构」，对应第 1 个义项：公司股份的持有人；句意为这位股东问董事会为什么利润没有分派出去。画面要点：会议室长桌、表决材料、持股凭证。

pos.zh: 股东；股份持有人（可指个人、基金或其他机构）

collocations.zh: 多数股东；持股过半的股东
积极干预公司治理的股东

derivatives.zh: 多处持股；持有的股份总额

senses.title: Owner of part of a company
senses.titleCN: 持有公司一部分股份的人
senses.definition: a person who owns one or more shares in a company
senses.definitionCN: 持有一家公司一份或多份股份的人
senses.example: Every shareholder receives a copy of the annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 每位股东都会收到一份年度报告。
senses.why: Share names a divided portion of something and holder names the one who keeps it, so the word literally means the keeper of a portion of the company.
senses.whyCN: share 指从整体中分出的一份，holder 指持有者，所以这个词字面上就是「公司某一份的持有者」。

senses.title: Holder of a controlling stake
senses.titleCN: 持股足以控制公司的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder whose stake is large enough to direct the company
senses.definitionCN: 持股比例大到足以左右公司决策的股东
senses.example: The controlling shareholder can appoint most of the board.
senses.exampleCN: 控股股东能够任命董事会的大部分成员。
senses.why: The same ownership relation is read by weight: when the held portion passes a threshold, the keeper of that portion gains the power to steer the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同样的持有关系按分量来读：当握有的那一份越过某个门槛，这一份的持有者就获得了左右整体的权力。

senses.title: Holder of a small stake
senses.definition: a shareholder whose stake is too small to influence control
senses.definitionCN: 持股比例较小、无法左右控制权的股东
senses.example: Minority shareholders joined forces to block the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 少数股东联合起来阻止这笔出售。
senses.why: Minority keeps the core meaning and adds scale: the portion is real but its weight is light, so the owner has a claim without command.
senses.whyCN: minority 保留核心义而补充了分量：那一份确实存在，但分量很轻，于是持有者有收益主张却没有指挥权。

senses.title: Institution as owner
senses.titleCN: 以机构身份持股的股东
senses.definition: a fund, pension scheme, insurer or other organization that holds shares
senses.definitionCN: 基金、养老金、保险公司等持有股份的组织
senses.example: Institutional shareholders pressed for clearer climate disclosures.
senses.exampleCN: 机构股东要求更清晰的气候信息披露。
senses.why: The holder here is not a single person but an organization acting as one legal owner, so the core sense is applied to a collective body.
senses.whyCN: 这里的持有者不是单个自然人，而是作为一个法律主体行事的组织，核心义因此落在一个集体身上。

senses.title: Private individual as owner
senses.titleCN: 以个人身份持股的股东
senses.definition: an ordinary private investor who owns shares directly
senses.definitionCN: 直接持有股份的普通个人投资者
senses.example: Retail shareholders often hold only a few dozen shares.
senses.exampleCN: 个人股东往往只持有几十股。
senses.why: Retail marks the opposite of institutional: the same legal relation is held in a private hand and on a small scale.
senses.whyCN: retail 标出与机构相反的一面：同样的法律关系握在私人手里，规模也小。

senses.title: Owner as a claim on value
senses.definition: the owner whose financial interest a company is said to serve
senses.definitionCN: 公司被说成应当为其财务利益服务的持股方
senses.example: The takeover was justified as a way to maximize shareholder value.
senses.exampleCN: 这场收购被辩解为最大化股东价值的手段。
senses.why: Once ownership is abstracted from a person to a financial claim, the shareholder becomes a stand-in for the value that the portion represents.
senses.whyCN: 当所有权从具体的人抽象成一项财务主张，股东就成了那一份所代表价值的代称。

senses.title: Voter in corporate governance
senses.titleCN: 在公司治理中投票的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder exercising voting rights at a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 在股东会议上行使表决权的持股人
senses.example: Shareholders voted against the proposed pay package.
senses.exampleCN: 股东投票否决了拟议的薪酬方案。
senses.why: A share carries a vote as well as a dividend, so the keeper of a portion also becomes a participant in deciding how the company is run.
senses.whyCN: 股份除了带来股息，也带来表决权，因此这一份的持有者同时成为公司如何运转的决策参与者。

senses.title: Activist owner pressing for change
senses.titleCN: 积极推动公司改变的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder who publicly campaigns to change company policy or leadership
senses.definitionCN: 公开推动公司改变政策或领导层的股东
senses.example: An activist shareholder nominated three new directors.
senses.exampleCN: 一位积极股东提名了三位新董事。
senses.why: Here the voting and value senses combine: the owner uses the stake as leverage to force a change rather than merely to receive a return.
senses.whyCN: 这里投票义与价值义合并：持有者把股份当作杠杆去迫使改变，而不只是领取回报。

intro.en: Shareholder is an English compound of share and holder, built from Old English material rather than borrowed from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: shareholder 是 share 与 holder 构成的英语复合词，用的是古英语材料，而非借自拉丁语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Scearu meant a division, portion or allotted part, and it is generally thought to be related to scieran 'to cut, shear', so a share is literally a piece cut off from a whole.
items.cn: scearu 意为「划分、份额、分得的部分」，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词，因此「一份」本义就是从整体上切下来的一块。

items.en: Healdan meant to hold, keep or watch over, and its agent form holder named the one who keeps something in hand.
items.cn: healdan 意为「持有、保管、看守」，其表人形式 holder 指把某物握在手中的人。

items.en: By the Middle English period holder was a settled noun for a person who possesses land, an office or an object.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，holder 已经是稳定的名词，指拥有土地、职位或物品的人。

items.en: Joint-stock companies divided their capital into transferable portions, and the compound shareholder named the person who kept one of those portions. The first recorded uses are dated to the early eighteenth century.
items.cn: 合股公司把资本分成可转让的份额，复合词 shareholder 便用来指持有其中一份的人。已知最早用例一般定在十八世纪早期。

items.en: Industrial finance widened the word to institutions and private savers alike, and later governance debates added the controlling, minority and activist readings.
items.cn: 工业化金融把这个词扩展到机构与个人储蓄者，后来的治理讨论又添上控股、少数与积极干预等读法。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to shareholder but differs in formation; the second group shares the idea of owning a stake without being the same word.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或构成上与 shareholder 相近，但构词不同；第二组同样表示「持有份额」，却不是同一个词。

entries.definition: A near synonym built on stock rather than share; American English prefers it, but the two words describe the same legal position.
entries.definitionCN: 用 stock 而非 share 构成的近义说法；美式英语更常用它，但两个词描述的是同一种法律地位。

entries.definition: Originally the holder of a bet or a stake in a wager, now any party affected by a company; a stakeholder need not own a single share.
entries.definitionCN: 原指赌注的持有者，现指受公司影响的任何一方；利益相关者未必持有一股股份。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym formed with owner; it stresses ownership rather than the act of holding.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的同义说法，用 owner 构成，强调所有权而不是「持有」这个动作。

entries.definition: A farmer who works land for a share of the crop; the share here is harvest, not capital, and the word has no connection with company ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 按收成份额耕种他人土地的人；这里的 share 指收成而非资本，与公司所有权无关。

entries.definition: Anyone who puts money into an asset hoping for a return; an investor may hold bonds or property and need not own shares.
entries.definitionCN: 把资金投入资产以求得回报的人；投资者可能持有债券或房产，未必持有股份。

entries.definition: A descriptive phrase for a holder of equity, used when the legal nature of the ownership matters more than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 对权益持有者的描述性说法，用于强调所有权的法律性质而非持有人本身。

entries.definition: In company law, especially British usage, a member is a person entered on the register of members, which in practice means a shareholder.
entries.definitionCN: 在公司法、尤其是英式用法中，member 指登记在公司成员名册上的人，实务上就是股东。

entries.definition: A party who acts for itself in a transaction, as opposed to an agent; the word marks a role in the deal, not ownership of shares.
entries.definitionCN: 在交易中代表自己行事的一方，与代理人相对；它标出交易角色，而不表示持有股份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Share plus holder: the person who holds one of the cut portions of a company.
normal.cn: share 加 holder：持有公司被切出的其中一份的人。

normal.en: The Old English noun behind share meant a division or allotted part, so ownership is pictured as holding a cut slice.
normal.cn: share 背后的古英语名词本义是划分或分得的部分，所以所有权可以想成握着一片切下来的份。

normal.en: Stockholder is the American twin; both point to the same register of owners.
normal.cn: stockholder 是美式英语里的对应词；两者指向同一份所有者名册。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the word by size and by owner type: majority, minority, controlling, institutional, activist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按规模与持有人类型给这个词分类：多数、少数、控股、机构、积极干预。

normal.en: A shareholder owns shares; a stakeholder merely has something at stake, which is the distinction to keep in mind.
normal.cn: shareholder 拥有股份；stakeholder 只是有利益牵涉，这个区别要记牢。

abstract.en: Picture a company as a pie cut into equal slices, with one slice wrapped in a document and kept in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 把公司想成一块切成等份的饼，其中一份用文件包好，收在口袋里。

abstract.en: Picture a voting card whose weight is set by how many slices the hand already holds.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表决卡，它的分量由那只手已经握住的份数决定。

abstract.en: Picture a claim on a stream of future profit, drawn as a thin line running from the company to a waiting hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一项对未来利润的权利，画成一条从公司流向等待之手的细线。

examples.en: The largest shareholder blocked the merger at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 最大股东在年度会议上阻止了这次合并。

examples.en: Shareholders expect the dividend to rise with profits.
examples.cn: 股东期待股息随利润一同提高。

examples.en: A pension fund can be a patient shareholder for many years.
examples.cn: 养老基金可以多年做一位有耐心的股东。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「share（一份）+ holder（持有者）」——持有公司一份的人 → 股东

root: share 出自古英语 scearu「划分、份额」，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词；holder 由 hold「持有」加表人后缀构成。整个词是英语本族复合词，不来自拉丁语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold from one relation: a person keeps a divided portion of a company, and that portion is then read by weight, by owner type, by value, by vote and by pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一种关系展开：一个人持有公司被分出的一份，这一份再按分量、持有人类型、价值、表决与施压等角度被读出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a company cut into equal slices, one slice held in a hand together with a voting card.
core.cn: 核心意象：公司被切成等份，一只手握着其中一份，同时拿着表决卡。

branches.en: BASE RELATION: the word itself is simply the keeper of one cut portion of the company.
branches.cn: 基础关系：这个词本身就是公司某一份的持有者。

branches.en: WEIGHT OF THE SLICE: a large portion can steer the whole, while a small portion can only object.
branches.cn: 那一份的分量：大份能左右整体，小份只能表示反对。

branches.en: WHO HOLDS IT: the same portion can rest in an organization or in a private hand.
branches.cn: 由谁持有：同一份既可以归机构，也可以归个人。

branches.en: VALUE CLAIM: ownership abstracted into the financial interest that the company is told to serve.
branches.cn: 价值主张：所有权被抽象为公司被要求去服务的财务利益。

branches.en: VOICE AND PRESSURE: the voting card turns the held portion into a say in how the company is run.
branches.cn: 表决与施压：表决卡把握有的那一份变成对公司运转的发言权。

intro.en: Shareholder is made of native English pieces, so its family is built by compounding and by the agent suffix rather than by Latin derivation.
intro.cn: shareholder 由英语本族成分构成，因此它的词族靠复合与表人后缀扩展，而不是靠拉丁语派生。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word lies behind this compound. Latin-based finance vocabulary enters English separately through words such as equity, capital and dividend.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词背后没有拉丁词。拉丁来源的金融词汇是通过 equity、capital、dividend 等词另行进入英语的。

items.structure: share (Old English noun, a division or portion)
items.meaning: a portion cut from a whole
items.example: Each child took a share of the fruit.
items.exampleCN: 每个孩子都分到了一份水果。

items.structure: hold (Old English verb, to keep or watch over)
items.example: She held the deed in her hand.

items.structure: -er (Old English agent suffix, one who does or keeps)
items.example: The keeper of the key opened the door.

items.meaning: the keeper of a portion of a company
items.example: A shareholder may vote at the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 股东可以在会议上投票。

items.meaning: the state or amount of holding shares
items.example: Her shareholding rose above ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 她的持股比例升到百分之十以上。

items.meaning: several blocks of shares held in different companies
items.meaningCN: 在不同公司持有的多笔股份
items.exampleCN: 他申报了自己全部持股。

items.meaning: the same legal owner, named through stock
items.meaningCN: 同一种法律所有者，只是用 stock 构成
items.exampleCN: 股东们批准了新董事会。

items.meaning: a party with an interest at stake
items.example: Local residents are stakeholders in the plan.
items.exampleCN: 当地居民是该计划的利益相关方。

items.meaningCN: 强调所有权的较少见同义说法

definition_en: shares in a company, or a stored supply of goods, animals or liquid; also a support or base

sceneCN: 这里指「存货、库存」，对应第 2 个义项：商家存放待售的商品；句意为仓库员工在冬季促销前清点存货。画面要点：货架、纸箱、盘点表。

senses.title: Shares in a company
senses.definition: the shares into which the ownership of a company is divided
senses.definitionCN: 公司所有权被分成的股份；股票
senses.example: She bought stock in a small software firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一家小型软件公司的股票。
senses.why: The financial sense grows from the image of a stored fund: capital kept by a company and divided into transferable units.
senses.whyCN: 金融义从「储存的资金」这一意象发展而来：公司保有的资本被分成可转让的单位。

senses.title: Goods kept for sale
senses.definition: the supply of goods that a shop or warehouse keeps ready for sale
senses.definitionCN: 商店或仓库备好待售的商品存货
senses.example: The shop ran out of stock before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在假期前就卖断了货。
senses.why: This is the most physical sense: things standing ready on shelves, held rather than used, exactly the notion of a stored supply.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的义项：货架上的东西备而不卖，正是「储存起来的供应」这一概念。

senses.title: Reserve supply
senses.definition: a supply of something kept in reserve for future need
senses.definitionCN: 为将来需要而留存的储备
senses.example: The city holds a stock of medical supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市储存了一批医疗物资。
senses.why: Goods become stock when they are set aside rather than consumed at once, so the sense widens from shop shelves to any reserve.
senses.whyCN: 物品一旦被留起来而不是马上消耗，就成了 stock；这一义项于是从商店货架扩展到任何储备。

senses.title: Farm animals
senses.definition: farm animals kept for meat, milk or work
senses.definitionCN: 为肉、奶或劳作而饲养的家畜
senses.example: The farmer moved his stock to higher ground.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把牲畜赶到地势更高的地方。
senses.why: Livestock are a living reserve: animals kept as a store of value and food, so the stored-supply image is applied to herds.
senses.whyCN: 家畜是活的储备：作为价值与食物的储存而饲养，因此「储存的供应」这一意象被用到畜群上。

senses.title: Cooking liquid base
senses.definition: a liquid in which bones, vegetables or meat have been simmered, used as a base for soups
senses.definitionCN: 用骨头、蔬菜或肉熬出的汤汁，作为汤菜底料
senses.example: Simmer the bones for hours to make a rich stock.
senses.exampleCN: 把骨头熬上几个小时，做成浓郁的原汤。
senses.why: A cook keeps this liquid standing ready as the base of many dishes, so the reserve sense shifts from solids to a saved liquid.
senses.whyCN: 厨师把这种汤汁常备着作为许多菜的基础，于是「储备」义从固体转到了留存的液体。

senses.title: Handle or support of a tool
senses.definition: the handle, butt or frame by which a tool or firearm is held
senses.definitionCN: 工具或枪械上供握持的柄、托或架
senses.example: He repaired the wooden stock of the old rifle.
senses.exampleCN: 他修好了那支旧步枪的木托。
senses.why: The oldest image returns literally: the stock is the upright piece that supports and is gripped, the base from which the rest extends.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象在这里字面回归：枪托或柄就是起支撑作用、供手握住的直立部件，是其余部分伸出的底座。

senses.title: Ancestry or descent
senses.definition: a person's family background or line of descent
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的家庭背景或血统来路
senses.example: She comes from farming stock.
senses.exampleCN: 她出身于务农的家庭。
senses.why: A family line is pictured as the trunk from which branches grow, so stock becomes the base from which a person descends.
senses.whyCN: 家族谱系被想象成生出枝干的主干，于是 stock 成了一个人所由来的根基。

senses.title: Rootstock for grafting
senses.definition: the rooted stem onto which another plant is grafted
senses.definitionCN: 接上另一株植物的带根茎干
senses.example: The apple variety was grafted onto a hardy stock.
senses.exampleCN: 这个苹果品种被嫁接到耐寒的砧木上。
senses.why: Here the stock is the supporting base in horticulture: the rooted part that holds up and feeds the scion above it.
senses.whyCN: 在园艺中，stock 就是承托的根基：带根的部分支撑并养活着上面的接穗。

senses.title: Standard or trite
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean standard, regularly used, or no longer fresh
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，表示常备的、惯用的或已不新鲜的
senses.example: The speech was full of stock phrases.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇演讲满是老套的说法。
senses.why: Goods kept in stock are the standard items always on hand, and from that comes the idea of an answer kept ready and therefore unoriginal.
senses.whyCN: 常备的货就是随时可取的常规品，由此引申出「备好的说法」，也就是不新鲜的套话。

intro.en: Stock goes back to an Old English word for a post or trunk, and its many senses radiate from that upright base. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stock 源自古英语表示木桩或树干的名词，众多义项都从这个直立的基底辐射出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stocc meant a stump, post, stake or tree trunk, the solid upright piece from which other things could grow or be supported.
items.cn: stocc 意为树桩、柱子、木桩或树干，是能长出他物或支撑他物的坚实直立部件。

items.en: The word is reconstructed as *stukkaz, the same family that gives German Stock and Dutch stok, all meaning a stick or trunk.
items.cn: 该词被重构为原始日耳曼语形式，意为棍棒或树干；德语 Stock 与荷兰语 stok 同属这一族。

items.en: The deeper Indo-European source of this Germanic word is source uncertain, and no reliable Latin cognate has been identified.
items.cn: 这个日耳曼词更早的印欧语来源不确定，也没有找到可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: By the thirteenth century stock also named a supply of goods or money kept on hand, as if goods stood stored around the base of a post.
items.cn: 到十三世纪，stock 也指手头存着的货物或资金，仿佛货物堆在木桩脚下备用。

items.en: Joint-stock companies of the seventeenth century treated their capital as a common stock divided into shares, which produced the modern financial sense.
items.cn: 十七世纪的合股公司把资本当作共同基金分成股份，由此产生了现代金融义。

items.en: The base image later yielded livestock as a living reserve, broth as a saved liquid, the stock of a gun as a handle and stock phrases as items kept ready.
items.cn: 这一基底意象后来又生出作为活储备的家畜、作为留存液体的原汤、作为握持部件的枪托，以及作为常备说法的套话。

note.en: The first group gathers short words that look or sound like stock; the second group shares one of its many meanings without being interchangeable everywhere.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音与 stock 相近的短词；第二组只共享它的某一个义项，并不能到处互换。

entries.definition: A neat pile of things, or to arrange them in a pile; the vowel is different and the word points to arrangement, not supply.
entries.definitionCN: 整齐的一堆，或把东西堆起来；元音不同，且指摆放方式而非储备。

entries.definition: A thin piece of wood, or to attach; it shares the trunk-and-branch image but is a different word in modern English.
entries.definitionCN: 细木条，或粘贴；它共享树干枝条的意象，但在现代英语中是另一个词。

entries.definition: The stem of a plant, or to follow prey quietly; the long vowel and the plant-stem image separate it from stock.
entries.definitionCN: 植物的茎，或悄悄跟踪猎物；长元音与植物茎的意象把它与 stock 区分开。

entries.definition: A covering for the foot; it ends in a single consonant sound and has no connection with supply or capital.
entries.definitionCN: 袜子；以单个辅音结尾，与储备或资本毫无关系。

entries.definition: Goods held for sale, usually with records of quantity and value; it is the accounting term for what a shop calls stock.
entries.definitionCN: 持有的待售商品，通常配有数量与价值记录；它是商店所说的 stock 在会计上的说法。

entries.definition: The amount of something available for use; supply can be flowing in, while stock is what is already held.
entries.definitionCN: 可供使用的数量；supply 可以是正在流入的量，而 stock 是已经握在手里的量。

entries.definition: Something kept back for future use, such as oil reserves; reserve stresses the act of holding back more than the goods themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 留待将来使用之物，如石油储量；reserve 更强调「留起来」的动作，而非货物本身。

entries.definition: The value of ownership in a company, treated as shares; it overlaps with stock in finance but belongs to a different vocabulary.
entries.definitionCN: 公司所有权的价值，以股份形式存在；在金融语境与 stock 重叠，但属于另一套词汇。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Germanic root, real compounds and real fixed phrases, with no invented rhyme.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的日耳曼词根、真实复合词与真实固定搭配，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: The core picture is an upright post or trunk, the base on which other things stand.
normal.cn: 核心画面是一根直立的木桩或树干，是其他东西赖以站立的基底。

normal.en: Goods standing ready around that base become a store, which is the bridge from post to inventory.
normal.cn: 堆在基底周围随时可取的货物成了储备，这是从木桩通往存货的桥梁。

normal.en: Company capital kept as a common fund becomes stock in the financial sense.
normal.cn: 公司保有作为共同基金的资本，就成了金融意义上的股票。

normal.en: Fixed phrases keep the physical sense visible: in stock, out of stock, take stock.
normal.cn: 固定搭配让具体义保持可见：有现货、缺货、盘点。

normal.en: The same base image explains the gun stock, the rootstock and the family stock.
normal.cn: 同一个基底意象解释了枪托、砧木与家族血统。

abstract.en: Picture a post in a yard with sacks of grain piled at its foot, waiting rather than being used.
abstract.cn: 想象院子里一根木桩，脚边堆着粮袋，只等着被用而不是立刻用掉。

abstract.en: Picture a trunk that sends up branches, so that the base is also the line of descent.
abstract.cn: 想象一根树干抽出枝条，于是基底同时也是血统的来路。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of standard answers kept ready for any occasion, which is how a phrase becomes stale.
abstract.cn: 想象一货架随时可取的标准答案，这正是套话变得陈腐的方式。

examples.en: The company issued new stock to fund the factory.
examples.cn: 公司发行新股为工厂筹措资金。

examples.en: We keep a stock of candles in case of a power cut.
examples.cn: 我们存了一批蜡烛，以防停电。

examples.en: The farmer sold half his stock at the autumn market.
examples.cn: 农民在秋季集市上卖掉了一半牲畜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木桩」立在那里当底座，周围堆着货 → 存货、储备；公司把资本存成一份份 → 股票

root: 古英语 stocc「树桩、柱子、树干」，属日耳曼语族，德语 Stock、荷兰语 stok 同源；更早的印欧语来源不确定，未发现可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one upright base: a post supports, goods stand stored around it, capital is kept as shares, herds are a living reserve, and a line of descent is the trunk of a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个直立基底辐射开来：木桩起支撑作用，货物围它存放，资本以股份形式保存，畜群是活的储备，血统则是一个家族的主干。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sturdy post standing in a yard, sacks piled at its foot and branches rising from its top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根结实的木桩立在院子里，脚边堆着货袋，顶端抽出枝条。

branches.en: ISSUED CAPITAL: the stored fund of a company is cut into transferable shares.
branches.cn: 发行的资本：公司储存的资金被切成可转让的股份。

branches.en: STORED SUPPLY: goods or reserves stand ready instead of being used at once.
branches.cn: 储存的供应：货物或储备备而不用，而不是立刻消耗。

branches.en: LIVING AND LIQUID STOCK: herds are a living reserve, and broth is a reserve drawn out as liquid.
branches.cn: 活的与液的储备：畜群是活的储备，原汤则是以液体形式取出的储备。

branches.en: SUPPORTING BASE: the handle of a tool and the rootstock of a graft both hold up what extends from them.
branches.cn: 承托的基底：工具的柄与嫁接的砧木都支撑着从它们伸出的部分。

branches.en: INHERITED AND FIXED: a family line is a trunk, while goods kept in stock turn into standard, unoriginal phrases.
branches.cn: 承袭与固定：家族血统是一根主干，而常备的货则变成标准却陈腐的说法。

intro.en: Stock is a native English noun that compounds freely, producing words for storage, ownership and livestock.
intro.cn: stock 是英语本族名词，能自由复合，构成表示储存、所有权与家畜的词。

latinIntro.en: The stock family is Germanic and has no Latin-derived relatives; Latin-based finance words such as capital belong to a separate vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: stock 一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁来源的同族词；capital 等拉丁系金融词属于另一套词汇。

items.meaning: a post, trunk or stored supply
items.meaningCN: 木桩、树干或储存的供应
items.example: The stock stood in the yard.

items.meaning: shares or supplies in the plural
items.meaningCN: 复数形式的股票或存货

items.meaning: a large reserve heaped up for future use
items.meaningCN: 为将来使用而大量囤积的储备
items.example: They stockpiled grain for the winter.

items.meaning: a room where goods are kept
items.example: The boxes are in the stockroom.

items.meaning: the counting of goods on hand
items.example: The shop closes for stocktaking each year.
items.exampleCN: 这家店每年关门盘点一次。

items.meaning: to keep more goods than can be sold
items.exampleCN: 这家连锁店冬装备货过量。

items.example: Staff restocked the shelves at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 员工在黎明时补满了货架。

items.meaning: farm animals kept as a living reserve
items.meaningCN: 作为活储备饲养的家畜

items.meaning: a first element meaning supply or share
items.meaningCN: 作复合词首成分，表示供应或股份
items.exampleCN: 库存管理让货架保持充足。

definition_zh: 股票市场；股票交易所；股市行情
definition_en: the market in which shares of companies are bought and sold
core_image: 一座喧闹的拍卖大厅，无数公司股份在报价声中易手
scene: 午后的交易大厅里，大屏幕上的指数快速下滑，经纪人纷纷抛售手中股份。The stock market fell sharply after the central bank raised interest rates.
sceneCN: 这里指「股票市场整体」，对应第 1 个义项：买卖公司股份的市场；句意为央行加息后股市大幅下跌。画面要点：交易大厅、行情大屏、下单电话。

pos.zh: 股票市场；股市（可指交易场所、交易体系或整体行情）

senses.title: The market where shares are traded
senses.definition: the system or place in which shares of public companies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 公开买卖公司股份的体系或场所
senses.example: Pension funds are major players in the stock market.
senses.exampleCN: 养老基金是股票市场的重要参与者。
senses.why: Stock supplies the object and market supplies the meeting place for exchange, so the compound names the arena where shares change hands.
senses.whyCN: stock 提供交易对象，market 提供交换的场所，复合词因此指股份易手的场域。

senses.title: The secondary market for listed shares
senses.titleCN: 已上市股份的二级交易市场
senses.definition: the market in which existing shares are traded after the company has listed them
senses.definitionCN: 公司上市之后，已有股份在投资者之间转手的市场
senses.example: Most trading on the stock market happens between investors, not with the company.
senses.exampleCN: 股票市场上的交易大多发生在投资者之间，而不是与公司本身进行。
senses.why: Once shares exist, the market lets owners exchange them without the company issuing anything new, so the arena becomes a second-hand market for claims.
senses.whyCN: 股份一旦存在，市场就让持有者在彼此之间交换，公司不再发行新东西，于是这个场域成了权利主张的二手市场。

senses.title: The level of prices at a time
senses.definition: the general level or direction of share prices at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻股份价格的总体水平或走向
senses.example: The stock market was up three percent by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到中午时股市上涨了三个百分点。
senses.why: Because the arena is visible mainly through its prices, the name shifts from the place to the number that the place produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个场域主要通过价格显现，于是名称从场所转到场所产生的数字上。

senses.title: The physical exchange building
senses.definition: the building or floor where dealers meet to trade shares
senses.definitionCN: 交易员聚集买卖股份的建筑或交易大厅
senses.example: Tourists photographed the old stock market on Wall Street.
senses.exampleCN: 游客在华尔街拍摄那座古老的证券交易所。
senses.why: Before screens, the market was a room full of shouted orders, so the compound keeps a literal architectural sense.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕时代之前，市场就是一间充满喊价的屋子，因此这个复合词仍保留字面的建筑义。

senses.title: A barometer of the economy
senses.titleCN: 作为经济晴雨表的股市
senses.definition: the stock market understood as an indicator of economic confidence
senses.definitionCN: 被当作经济信心指标的股票市场
senses.example: Policymakers watch the stock market for signs of panic.
senses.exampleCN: 政策制定者观察股市以寻找恐慌迹象。
senses.why: Prices aggregate many people's expectations, so the arena is read as a signal about the wider economy rather than only about companies.
senses.whyCN: 价格汇总了许多人的预期，于是这个场域被读成关于更广经济的信号，而不只是关于公司。

senses.title: The global network of exchanges
senses.titleCN: 全球各交易所组成的网络
senses.definition: the worldwide system of linked exchanges trading shares around the clock
senses.definitionCN: 全球各地交易所在不同时区连成的股份交易体系
senses.example: A shock in one stock market spreads to others within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个股市的震荡会在数小时内传到其他股市。
senses.why: When many local arenas are connected by information and capital flows, the singular name stands for the whole network.
senses.whyCN: 当许多地方场域被信息与资本流动连在一起，单数的名称就代表整个网络。

senses.title: A speculative arena
senses.definition: the stock market seen as a place of speculation, euphoria and sudden loss
senses.definitionCN: 被视为投机、狂热与骤然亏损之所的股市
senses.example: He lost his savings in the stock market.
senses.exampleCN: 他在股市里赔掉了积蓄。
senses.why: The arena language invites a figurative reading in which traders are players and prices are bets, so the word can name a gamble.
senses.whyCN: 「场域」的说法引出比喻读法：交易者是玩家，价格是赌注，于是这个词也能指一场赌博。

senses.title: Public judgement of company value
senses.titleCN: 对公司价值的公开评判
senses.definition: the daily public assessment of what companies are worth
senses.definitionCN: 每天由市场给出的公司价值评估
senses.example: The stock market valued the startup at twice its sales.
senses.exampleCN: 股市给这家初创公司的估值达到其销售额的两倍。
senses.why: Each trade is a small verdict on value, so the arena becomes a continuous public judgement rather than a mere meeting place.
senses.whyCN: 每一笔交易都是对价值的一次小裁决，于是这个场域成了持续的公开评判，而不只是会面之处。

intro.en: Stock market joins two words of different origins: a Germanic stock for the shares and a Latin market for the place of trade. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stock market 把两个来源不同的词拼在一起：表示股份的日耳曼语 stock，与表示交易场所的拉丁语 market。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stock first meant a post or trunk and later a stored fund; in finance it came to mean the capital of a company divided into shares.
items.cn: stock 最初指木桩或树干，后来指储存的资金；在金融中转而指被分成股份的公司资本。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise', the source of merchant and mercantile.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或集市，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「商品」，也是 merchant 与 mercantile 的来源。

items.en: Market entered English through Old North French and settled as the ordinary word for a place where buyers and sellers meet.
items.cn: market 经古北法语进入英语，逐渐固定为买卖双方会面之处的常用词。

items.en: The compound stock market is generally dated to the early nineteenth century, when organized exchanges and daily share lists became common.
items.cn: 复合词 stock market 一般定在十九世纪早期，当时有组织的交易所与每日股价表开始普及。

items.en: Electronic trading detached the market from any single floor and made the singular name stand for a worldwide network.
items.cn: 电子交易把市场与任何单一交易大厅分开，使单数名称代表一个全球网络。

note.en: The first group contains phrases that look nearly identical but point to the exchange or the place rather than the market as a whole; the second group names the same arena from other vocabularies.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来几乎相同、却指交易所或场所而非整体市场的说法；第二组用别的词汇指同一场域。

entries.definition: The organized institution that runs trading in shares; it is the venue and operator, while the stock market is the wider activity and price level.
entries.definitionCN: 组织股份交易的有形机构；它指场所与运营者，而股票市场指更广的交易活动与价格水平。

entries.definition: Any place, physical or digital, where buyers and sellers meet; it lacks the specific link to company shares.
entries.definitionCN: 任何实体或数字的买卖双方会面之处；不含与公司股份的具体联系。

entries.definition: The shares themselves; the market is the arena, while stock is what is traded inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 股份本身；market 是场域，stock 是场域中被交易的东西。

entries.definition: A general system of exchange; alone it can mean any trade in goods, services or labour.
entries.definitionCN: 一般的交换体系；单独使用时可以指任何商品、服务或劳动力的交易。

entries.definition: The market for equity, meaning shares; it is the formal finance term for the same arena.
entries.definitionCN: 权益即股份的市场；这是同一场域的正式金融说法。

entries.definition: A common synonym in Australian and New Zealand usage, built on share instead of stock.
entries.definitionCN: 澳大利亚与新西兰常用的同义说法，用 share 而不是 stock 构成。

entries.definition: A continental European stock exchange, especially in French-speaking countries; it names an institution rather than the abstract market.
entries.definitionCN: 欧洲大陆的证券交易所，尤指法语地区；它指机构而非抽象市场。

entries.definition: The market for long-term funds, including both shares and bonds; the stock market is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 长期资金市场，包括股票与债券；股票市场只是其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound, real synonyms and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词两个真实的组成部分、真实同义词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Stock is what is traded; market is where it is traded, so the phrase is transparent.
normal.cn: stock 是被交易的东西，market 是交易发生的地方，所以这个短语一目了然。

normal.en: Stock itself began as a post or trunk and later became stored capital, which is why shares are called stock.
normal.cn: stock 本指木桩或树干，后来变成储存的资本，股份因此被称为 stock。

normal.en: Market comes from a Latin word for trade, the same source as merchant and mercantile.
normal.cn: market 出自拉丁语表示交易词，与 merchant、mercantile 同源。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show its force: crash, rally, index, bubble.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它的力度：崩盘、反弹、指数、泡沫。

normal.en: Stock exchange is the institution; stock market is the activity and the price level.
normal.cn: 证券交易所是机构，股票市场是活动与价格水平。

abstract.en: Picture a vast room where every shout is a tiny verdict on what a company is worth.
abstract.cn: 想象一间巨大的厅堂，每一声喊价都是对公司价值的一次微小裁决。

abstract.en: Picture prices as weather over that room, rising and falling while the floor stays fixed.
abstract.cn: 把价格想成那间厅堂上空的天气，起伏变化而地面不动。

abstract.en: Picture the room dissolving into screens, so the place becomes a network without walls.
abstract.cn: 想象厅堂化入屏幕，场所于是变成没有围墙的网络。

examples.en: The stock market reacted calmly to the election result.
examples.cn: 股市对选举结果反应平静。

examples.en: Small investors can now enter the stock market through apps.
examples.cn: 小投资者现在可以通过应用程序进入股市。

examples.en: A falling stock market often precedes a slowdown in hiring.
examples.cn: 股市下跌往往先于招聘放缓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stock（股份）+ market（市场）」——买卖股份的市场 → 股票市场

root: stock 出自古英语 stocc「木桩、树干」，后来指储存的资本与股份；market 出自拉丁语 mercatus「交易、集市」，经古北法语进入英语。两者在十九世纪初合成 stock market。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the arena itself to its prices, its buildings, its economic signal, its global network and finally to its speculative and judgemental force.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从场域本身出发，依次转到价格、建筑、经济信号、全球网络，最后落到投机与评判的力量上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowded trading floor where every shouted order is a small verdict on value.
core.cn: 核心意象：拥挤的交易大厅，每一次喊单都是对价值的一次小裁决。

branches.en: THE ARENA: the market is first the meeting place where listed shares change hands.
branches.cn: 场域：市场首先是已上市股份易手的会面之处。

branches.en: PRICE LEVEL: the place is then read through the number it produces each day.
branches.cn: 价格水平：场所再通过它每天产生的数字被读取。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: before screens, the arena was a literal room with a floor and a crowd.
branches.cn: 建筑：屏幕时代之前，场域就是一间有地面、有人群的真实屋子。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND NETWORK: many local arenas linked together become a barometer and a worldwide system.
branches.cn: 信号与网络：许多地方场域连在一起，成了晴雨表与全球体系。

branches.en: GAMBLE AND VERDICT: the same arena can be a place of speculation or a continuous public judgement of worth.
branches.cn: 博弈与裁决：同一场域既可以是投机之地，也可以是对价值的持续公开评判。

latinIntro.en: Market descends from Latin mercatus, which also gives merchant, mercantile and commerce.
latinIntro.cn: market 源自拉丁语 mercatus，merchant、mercantile 与 commerce 也出自这一支。

definition_zh: 一份；份额；股份；分享；共用；分配
definition_en: a portion of something, or to divide and use something with others
core_image: 一块饼被切成几份，几只手同时伸向同一份
scene: 两姐妹合住一套离车站不远的小公寓，分摊房租和水电。The sisters share a small flat near the station.
sceneCN: 这里指「共同使用」，对应第 4 个义项：与他人一起使用某物；句意为两姐妹合用车站附近的一套小公寓。画面要点：公寓钥匙、两人共用的餐桌、分摊账单。

pos.zh: 一份；份额；股份；市场占有率
分享；共用；分配；具有（共同特征）；转发

senses.title: A portion of a whole
senses.definition: a part or portion of something that is divided among people
senses.definitionCN: 某物被分给众人时的一份或一部分
senses.example: Each worker received a share of the profits.
senses.exampleCN: 每位工人都分到了一份利润。
senses.why: The word begins as a cut piece: something whole is divided, and one of the resulting portions is a share.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义是切下来的一块：整体被分开，分出来的其中一块就是一份。

senses.title: One unit of company ownership
senses.titleCN: 公司所有权的一个单位
senses.definition: one of the equal units into which a company's capital is divided
senses.definitionCN: 公司资本被分成的等份单位之一
senses.example: He sold his shares before the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 他在合并前卖掉了股份。
senses.why: Company capital is treated as a whole divided into equal portions, so the general idea of a portion becomes the financial unit of ownership.
senses.whyCN: 公司资本被当作整体分成等份，于是「一份」的一般概念成了金融上的所有权单位。

senses.title: To divide among people
senses.definition: to divide something into parts and give them to different people
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成几份交给不同的人
senses.example: They shared the prize money equally.
senses.exampleCN: 他们平分了奖金。
senses.why: As a verb the word performs the cutting: the whole is turned into portions and handed out.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，这个词执行「切分」：把整体变成几份并分发出去。

senses.title: To use jointly
senses.definition: to use, occupy or have something together with others
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起使用、居住或拥有某物
senses.example: The cousins share a flat near the university.
senses.exampleCN: 表亲们合用大学附近的一套公寓。
senses.why: Joint use means each person holds a portion of the same thing at the same time, so the divided portions overlap instead of separating.
senses.whyCN: 共同使用意味着每个人同时握有同一事物的一份，被分出的份额于是重叠而不是分开。

senses.title: To tell others something personal
senses.titleCN: 把私人的事说给别人听
senses.definition: to tell someone about your thoughts, feelings or news
senses.definitionCN: 把想法、感受或消息告诉别人
senses.example: She shared the news with her closest friend.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这个消息告诉了她最亲密的朋友。
senses.why: Information is treated as a possession that can be divided: to share it is to give another person a portion of what you hold.
senses.whyCN: 信息被当作可以分割的持有物：分享就是让别人得到你所持有内容的一份。

senses.title: To have in common
senses.definition: to have the same quality, interest or experience as another person
senses.definitionCN: 与别人具有相同的性质、兴趣或经历
senses.example: The two writers share a love of cold landscapes.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位作家都喜爱寒冷的风景。
senses.why: Here the portion is a quality that both people hold at once, so sharing means occupying the same ground rather than handing something over.
senses.whyCN: 这里的一份是两人同时拥有的性质，分享因此指站在同一块地面上，而不是把东西交出去。

senses.title: A company's portion of a market
senses.titleCN: 公司在市场总量中的份额
senses.definition: the part of total sales in a market held by one company or product
senses.definitionCN: 某一公司或产品在市场总销量中占的部分
senses.example: The brand gained market share in Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 该品牌在亚洲赢得了市场份额。
senses.why: The general portion sense is measured against a market instead of a company, so share becomes the slice of total demand that a seller controls.
senses.whyCN: 一般「一份」义改为以市场而非公司为整体来衡量，份额于是成了卖方控制的那一片总需求。

senses.title: To distribute in portions
senses.definition: to divide something out among a group, often with the particle out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物按份分给一群人，常与 out 连用
senses.example: The teacher shared out the books among the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把书分给了全班。
senses.why: The particle out completes the cutting image: the whole is visibly split and each portion leaves the centre.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 out 补全了切分的意象：整体被明确切开，每一份都离开中心。

senses.title: To repost content online
senses.definition: to repost a piece of content so that others in a network can see it
senses.definitionCN: 把一条内容转发出去，让网络中的其他人看到
senses.example: Thousands of users shared the video overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 成千上万的用户在夜里转发了这段视频。
senses.why: Digital sharing keeps the old geometry: a copy leaves your screen and becomes a portion held by many other screens at once.
senses.whyCN: 数字转发保留了旧有的几何关系：一份拷贝离开你的屏幕，成为许多其他屏幕同时持有的一份。

intro.en: Share is a native English noun and verb whose core is a cut-off portion. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: share 是英语本族名词兼动词，核心意思是切下来的一份。年代均为约数。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as a West Germanic word for a division or allotted part, from a root meaning to cut.
items.cn: 其祖词被重构为西日耳曼语中表示划分或分得部分的词，出自意为「切」的词根。

items.en: Scearu meant a division, portion or share, and it is generally thought to be related to scieran 'to cut, shear'.
items.cn: scearu 意为划分、份额，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词。

items.en: The form settled as share, naming a portion of food, land or money allotted to someone.
items.cn: 形式固定为 share，指分给某人的一份食物、土地或钱财。

items.en: When capital was divided into transferable portions, the noun extended from food and land to ownership in a company.
items.cn: 当资本被分成可转让的份额，这个名词便从食物与土地扩展到公司所有权。

items.en: Modern English adds market share and online sharing, applying the portion image to demand and to digital copies.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上市场份额与网络转发，把「一份」的意象用到需求与数字拷贝上。

note.en: The first group is built on similar sounds and spellings; the second group contains words for a portion or for dividing that differ in emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组建立在相近的读音与拼写上；第二组是表示「一份」或「分配」的词，侧重点不同。

entries.definition: To cut wool or metal with a blade; it is the cutting verb behind the portion noun and is not interchangeable with it.
entries.definitionCN: 用刀刃剪羊毛或切金属；它是「份额」名词背后的切割动词，不能与之互换。

entries.definition: The land at the edge of water, or to support something; the vowel is longer and the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 水边陆地，或支撑某物；元音更长，意义无关。

entries.definition: A sharp broken piece of glass or pottery; it is a fragment, but not a portion allotted to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 玻璃或陶器的尖利碎片；它是碎片，但不是分给人的一份。

entries.definition: A seat for one person; it begins with a different consonant and has no connection with portion or division.
entries.definitionCN: 单人座椅；开头辅音不同，与份额或划分无关。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, especially of food or an amount; it is more neutral and less financial than share.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的一部分，尤指食物或数量；比 share 更中性，金融色彩更少。

entries.definition: The broad everyday word for a piece of a whole; share adds the idea of an allotted or legitimate portion.
entries.definitionCN: 表示整体一部分的日常通用词；share 另含「分得、应得」的意思。

entries.definition: An interest or share in a business, often implying risk; a stake can be held without owning formal shares.
entries.definitionCN: 对企业的利益或份额，常含风险意味；持有 stake 未必拥有正式股份。

entries.definition: A fixed amount that must be contributed or may be received; it emphasizes a rule or limit, not a cut portion.
entries.definitionCN: 必须贡献或可以领取的固定数量；强调规则或限额，而非切分的一份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real cutting root, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的切割词根、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Share is a cut piece: the whole is divided and one portion goes to each person.
normal.cn: share 是切下来的一块：整体被分开，每人得到一份。

normal.en: The related cutting verb survives in shear, which cuts wool from a sheep.
normal.cn: 同族的切割动词还留在 shear 里，指从羊身上剪下羊毛。

normal.en: Company capital divided into equal pieces gives the financial sense of shares.
normal.cn: 公司资本分成等份，产生了金融意义上的股份。

normal.en: Fixed phrases reveal the range: market share, share price, fair share, share out.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示范围：市场份额、股价、应得的一份、分发。

normal.en: Social media sharing is still giving others a copy, a digital portion of what you hold.
normal.cn: 社交媒体上的转发仍然是让别人得到一份拷贝，也就是你所持内容的数字份额。

abstract.en: Picture a round loaf cut into wedges, with a different hand taking each wedge.
abstract.cn: 想象一只圆面包切成扇形块，不同的人各取一块。

abstract.en: Picture several hands resting on the same wedge at once, which is joint use.
abstract.cn: 想象几只手同时按在同一块上，这就是共同使用。

abstract.en: Picture the same wedge copied onto many screens, so one portion becomes many portions.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块被复制到许多屏幕上，一份于是变成许多份。

examples.en: The two countries share a long river border.
examples.cn: 两国共享一条长长的河流边界。

examples.en: She bought a hundred shares in the airline.
examples.cn: 她买入了这家航空公司一百股股份。

examples.en: Parents should share housework instead of dividing it by gender.
examples.cn: 父母应当分担家务，而不是按性别划分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「切片」——把整块切成几份，人人拿一份 → 份额；把同一份交给别人一起用 → 分享

root: 古英语 scearu「划分、份额」，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词，出自意为「切」的词根；由食物与土地的一份扩展到公司股份与市场份额。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the act of cutting: a whole becomes one portion, portions become ownership units, and the verb then divides, uses jointly, confides, finds common ground and reposts.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着切分动作展开：整体变成一份，份变成所有权单位，动词再引申出分配、共用、倾诉、共同之处与转发。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round loaf cut into wedges, several hands reaching for one wedge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只圆面包切成扇形块，几只手同时伸向其中一块。

branches.en: PORTION MEASURED: a share is a cut portion, whether of food or of a whole market.
branches.cn: 被衡量的份：无论食物还是整个市场，share 都是切出来的一份。

branches.en: DIVIDE OUT: as a verb the word cuts the whole and hands each portion to someone.
branches.cn: 分出去：作动词时把整体切开，把每一份交给人。

branches.en: HOLD TOGETHER AND PASS ON: joint use, confiding and reposting all give another person a portion of what you hold.
branches.cn: 共持与传递：共用、倾诉与转发都是让别人得到你所持内容的一份。

branches.en: CAPITAL UNIT: company capital is cut into equal portions that can be owned and sold.
branches.cn: 资本单位：公司资本被切成可拥有、可出售的等份。

branches.en: SAME GROUND: two people hold one quality at once, so sharing becomes having in common.
branches.cn: 同一块地面：两人同时拥有一种性质，分享于是变成共有。

intro.en: Share compounds and derives freely, producing words for holders, for joint use and for allotment.
intro.cn: share 能自由复合与派生，构成表示持有者、共用与分配的词。

latinIntro.en: The share family is native English and has no Latin-derived relatives; financial Latin vocabulary such as equity and capital enters separately.
latinIntro.cn: share 一族属英语本族，没有拉丁来源的同族词；equity、capital 等拉丁系金融词汇是另行进入的。

items.meaning: a person who gives a portion

items.meaning: fit to be passed to others

items.example: The share-out of the land took weeks.

items.example: Sharecroppers kept a third of the cotton.
items.exampleCN: 分成制农民留下三分之一的棉花。

items.exampleCN: 这个工具最初是共享软件。

definition_en: a debt security, or a close connection that ties people or things together
core_image: 一条绳子把两块木头系在一起，绳结既是连接也是约束
scene: 两个相邻小镇因一年一度的联合节庆而人情日益紧密，居民互相帮忙修屋。A strong bond between the two towns grew out of the annual festival.
sceneCN: 这里指「人与人之间的纽带」，对应第 2 个义项：把人们联系在一起的亲密关系；句意为两镇之间的紧密纽带源自一年一度的节庆。画面要点：两镇横幅、共同搭建的摊位、握手的人。

pos.zh: 债券；纽带；契约；化学键；保释金；保税状态
黏合；结合；建立感情联系

senses.title: A debt security
senses.definition: a certificate of borrowing in which an investor lends money and is repaid with interest
senses.definitionCN: 投资者借出资金、到期收回本金并收取利息的借款凭证
senses.example: The city issued a bond to build the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市发行债券来修建新桥。
senses.why: The word for a tie becomes a word for a written obligation: the document binds the borrower to repay, so the instrument is itself a bond.
senses.whyCN: 表示「束缚」的词转成书面债务：文件把借款人约束在还款义务上，这份凭证本身就是一个 bond。

senses.title: A close personal tie
senses.titleCN: 人与人之间的紧密联系
senses.definition: a close relationship that connects people emotionally
senses.definitionCN: 在情感上把人们联系起来的亲密关系
senses.example: A lasting bond formed between the two families.
senses.exampleCN: 两个家庭之间形成了持久的纽带。
senses.why: This is the image at its plainest: two separate things held together by a tie that neither can easily break.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的意象：两样分开的东西被一条不易断的绳子系在一起。

senses.title: A binding promise
senses.titleCN: 有约束力的承诺或契约
senses.definition: a formal promise or agreement that cannot be broken without consequence
senses.definitionCN: 一旦作出便不能随意违反的正式承诺或协议
senses.example: The two firms signed a bond to share the research costs.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司签署契约共同承担研究费用。
senses.why: A bond is a tie made by words: the promise fastens the parties to a future action.
senses.whyCN: bond 是用言语打成的结：承诺把各方系在一项未来的行动上。

senses.title: To join materials
senses.definition: to fasten two materials together with glue or heat
senses.definitionCN: 用胶或热把两种材料固定在一起
senses.example: The carpenter bonded the two panels with resin.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠用树脂把两块板黏合起来。
senses.why: As a verb, the tie becomes an action: two surfaces are made to hold as one.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，绳索变成动作：两个表面被弄得像一体那样保持在一起。

senses.title: To form an emotional attachment
senses.definition: to develop a close relationship with a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 与人或动物建立起亲密关系
senses.example: The child bonded with the rescue dog within days.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子在几天内就和那只救助犬亲近起来。
senses.why: The physical verb is applied inward: two lives are fastened by feeling rather than by glue.
senses.whyCN: 具体的黏合动作转向内心：两条生命由情感而不是胶水系在一起。

senses.title: A chemical bond
senses.definition: the force that holds atoms together in a molecule
senses.definitionCN: 把原子结合成分子的作用力
senses.example: Water forms because of the bond between hydrogen and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 水因氢与氧之间的化学键而形成。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the plain image: atoms are the two things, and the bond is the tie that keeps them together.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了这个朴素意象：原子是两样东西，化学键是把它们系住的绳索。

senses.title: Goods held under customs bond
senses.definition: goods kept in a bonded warehouse until customs duty is paid
senses.definitionCN: 存放在保税仓、待缴关税后再放行的货物
senses.example: The wine stayed in bond until the duty was paid.
senses.exampleCN: 这批葡萄酒一直保税存放，直到缴清关税。
senses.why: Here the tie is legal rather than physical: the goods are bound to the warehouse and cannot leave before the duty is settled.
senses.whyCN: 这里的束缚是法律而非物理的：货物被系在仓库上，关税未结清就不能离开。

senses.title: A bail bond or surety
senses.definition: money or a promise given to secure a person's release from custody
senses.definitionCN: 为使被拘者获释而交纳的金钱或作出的担保
senses.example: He was released after posting a bond.
senses.exampleCN: 他交纳保释金后获释。
senses.why: The promise ties a person to appearing in court, so the money is a visible knot that can be forfeited if the tie is broken.
senses.whyCN: 承诺把人系在出庭义务上，那笔钱就是看得见的绳结，一旦断裂便会被没收。

intro.en: Bond came into English from Old Norse and was reinforced by a native word for a fetter; both trace to one Germanic verb meaning to bind. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bond 从古诺斯语进入英语，并与本族表示「束缚」的词并用；两者都追溯到同一个意为「捆绑」的日耳曼动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Band meant a cord or band used to tie things together, and it entered English during the Norse period.
items.cn: band 意为用来系住东西的绳或带，在北欧语影响时期进入英语。

items.en: Old English bend meant a bond or fetter, so the native word reinforced the borrowed one in the same meaning.
items.cn: 古英语 bend 意为束缚、镣铐，本族词以同一意义强化了借来的词。

items.en: Both point to a Germanic verb reconstructed as *bindanan 'to bind', which also yields bind and binding.
items.cn: 两者都指向被重构为「捆绑」的日耳曼动词，bind 与 binding 也由此而来。

items.en: By the Middle English period a bond was a written obligation that legally tied a person to pay or perform.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，bond 已指有法律约束力的书面义务，把某人系在付款或履约上。

items.en: Governments and companies began issuing transferable bonds, turning the legal document into a traded debt security.
items.cn: 政府与公司开始发行可转让债券，把法律文书变成可交易的债务证券。

items.en: Chemists borrowed the word for the force that ties atoms, and the same period produced bonded warehouses for goods held under customs control.
items.cn: 化学家借这个词表示把原子系住的作用力；同一时期又出现保税仓，用来存放受海关监管的货物。

note.en: The first group contains short words that look or sound like bond; the second group holds near neighbours from the vocabularies of relationships, finance and joining.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音与 bond 相近的短词；第二组来自关系、金融与结合三套词汇。

entries.definition: A strip that ties things, or a group of people; it shares the tying image but is a distinct word with a different vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 捆系的带子，或一群人；共享捆系意象，但元音不同，是另一个词。

entries.definition: To tie or fasten; it is the action that a bond performs, not the tie itself.
entries.definitionCN: 捆绑、系住；它是 bond 所执行的动作，而不是绳索本身。

entries.definition: The past form of bind, and also an adjective meaning tied or certain; bound is a form or state, while bond is the tie.
entries.definitionCN: bind 的过去形式，也作形容词表示被束缚或必定；bound 是形式或状态，bond 是绳索。

entries.definition: A hard part of a skeleton; it differs in vowel and has no connection with tying or debt.
entries.definitionCN: 骨骼的坚硬部分；元音不同，与捆绑或债务无关。

entries.definition: A connection between people or things; it is the everyday word for what bond says in a warmer or more formal register.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物之间的联系；是 bond 更温暖或更正式语域下的日常说法。

entries.definition: A connection between two things, often mechanical or logical; link stresses joining, while bond stresses holding fast.
entries.definitionCN: 两物之间的连接，常指机械或逻辑联系；link 强调连接，bond 强调系紧。

entries.definition: A formal debt instrument, usually unsecured; it overlaps with bond in finance but is a narrower legal term.
entries.definitionCN: 通常无担保的正式债务凭证；金融上与 bond 重叠，但法律含义更窄。

entries.definition: Any tradable financial instrument, including bonds and shares; a bond is one kind of security.
entries.definitionCN: 任何可交易的金融工具，包括债券与股票；bond 是证券的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Germanic root shared with bind, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：与 bind 共享的真实日耳曼词根、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Bond and bind are one family: the noun is the tie, the verb is the act of tying.
normal.cn: bond 与 bind 同属一族：名词是绳索，动词是系的动作。

normal.en: A written promise ties a borrower to repayment, which is why a debt certificate is called a bond.
normal.cn: 书面承诺把借款人系在还款上，债务凭证因此被称为债券。

normal.en: Chemistry uses the plain image: atoms are separate things, and the bond is the tie between them.
normal.cn: 化学沿用朴素意象：原子是分开的东西，化学键是它们之间的绳索。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the finance sense: government bond, corporate bond, bond yield.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金融义：政府债券、公司债券、债券收益率。

normal.en: Bonded goods are legally tied to a warehouse until duty is paid.
normal.cn: 保税货物在法律上被系在仓库上，直到缴清关税。

abstract.en: Picture two planks joined by a single rope knot that neither side can untie alone.
abstract.cn: 想象两块木板被一个绳结系住，任何一方都无法独自解开。

abstract.en: Picture the rope becoming invisible and passing between two people as trust.
abstract.cn: 想象那条绳子变得看不见，作为信任穿过两个人之间。

abstract.en: Picture the same knot redrawn as a line between two atoms, or as a signature on a debt.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个绳结被改画成两个原子之间的线，或债务上的一枚签名。

examples.en: The museum bought a rare bond from the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 博物馆买下了一张十八世纪的珍稀债券。

examples.en: Music created a bond between the two strangers.
examples.cn: 音乐在两位陌生人之间建立了纽带。

examples.en: The glue bonds the layers into one strong sheet.
examples.cn: 胶把各层黏合成一张坚固的板。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「绑的」——用绳子绑在一起 → 纽带、结合；把还款义务绑在纸上 → 债券

root: 古诺斯语 band「绳索、带子」与古英语 bend「束缚」合并而成，二者都出自意为「捆绑」的日耳曼动词，与 bind 同族；先指法律约束，再指债券与化学键。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all depend on one image: a tie. Two things are held together, then a promise holds a person to a duty, then a document holds a borrower to repayment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都依赖同一个意象：绳索。两样东西被系在一起，随后承诺把人系在义务上，文书又把借款人系在还款上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one rope knot joining two planks, a connection that is also a restraint.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个绳结把两块木板系在一起，连接同时也是约束。

branches.en: DEBT DOCUMENT: a written tie that holds a borrower to repayment turns into a traded security.
branches.cn: 债务文书：把借款人系在还款上的书面绳索，变成了可交易的证券。

branches.en: PERSONAL TIE: the plainest reading, two people fastened by feeling.
branches.cn: 人际纽带：最朴素的读法，两个人由情感系在一起。

branches.en: PLEDGE AND SURETY: a promise binds a person to a future act, and bail money makes that tie visible.
branches.cn: 承诺与担保：承诺把人系在未来的行动上，保释金让这条绳索看得见。

branches.en: JOINING: the tie becomes an action, gluing surfaces or attaching two lives.
branches.cn: 结合：绳索变成动作，黏合表面或连接两条生命。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN TIES: atoms are held by a chemical link, goods are held by a customs bond.
branches.cn: 非人的束缚：原子由化学键系住，货物由保税监管系住。

intro.en: Bond belongs to the bind family, so its compounds and derived words circle around tying, obligation and attachment.
intro.cn: bond 属于 bind 一族，其复合词与派生词都围绕捆系、义务与依恋展开。

latinIntro.en: The bond family is Germanic; Latin contributes separate words such as obligare, from which obligation is borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: bond 一族属日耳曼语；拉丁语另以 obligare 等词贡献了 obligation 一类的借词。

items.example: The bond held the planks together.

items.meaning: the act of joining or forming attachment
items.meaningCN: 黏合或建立依恋的行为
items.example: Bonding takes time for adopted pets.
items.exampleCN: 被领养的宠物需要时间建立依恋。

items.meaning: joined, or held under customs bond
items.example: Bonded goods wait in the warehouse.
Bondholders receive interest twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 债券持有人每年收取两次利息。

items.meaning: the state of being tied or enslaved
items.example: The novel describes years of bondage.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描写了多年的奴役。

items.meaning: able to be joined or insured
items.example: The fabric is bondable under heat.
They bind the pages by hand.

items.meaning: the cover of a book, or a rule that must be obeyed
items.meaningCN: 书籍装订，或有约束力的规定
items.exampleCN: 这份协议具有法律约束力。

items.meaning: a strip used to tie, or a group
items.meaningCN: 用来捆系的带子，或一群人
items.example: A rubber band held the papers.
items.exampleCN: 一根橡皮筋把纸张束住。

definition_zh: 证券；可交易的金融工具（股票、债券等）
definition_en: tradable financial instruments, such as shares and bonds
core_image: 一叠盖着印章的凭证，每一张都能在市场上换成钱
scene: 听证会上，监管人员指出这家公司向公众出售可交易的投资凭证时没有充分披露风险。The regulator accused the firm of selling securities without proper disclosure.
sceneCN: 这里指「可交易的金融工具」，对应第 1 个义项：股票、债券等可在市场上买卖的凭证；句意为监管者指控该公司出售证券时未充分披露信息。画面要点：成叠凭证、监管徽章、披露文件。

pos.zh: 证券（复数形式，统指股票、债券等可交易金融工具）

derivatives.zh: 安全；保障；单数形式的证券
把资产打包成可交易证券

senses.title: Tradable financial instruments as a class
senses.titleCN: 作为一类可交易金融工具
senses.definition: financial instruments that can be bought and sold in markets, such as shares and bonds
senses.definitionCN: 可在市场上买卖的金融工具，如股票与债券
senses.example: Banks must hold enough capital against their securities.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须为其证券持有足够的资本。
senses.why: The plural of security names instruments that make an investor feel secure because they can be sold or redeemed; the abstract assurance becomes a countable paper claim.
senses.whyCN: security 的复数指那些因可出售或可兑付而让投资者安心的工具；抽象的保障于是变成可计数的纸面权利。

senses.title: Debt securities
senses.definition: instruments that represent a loan to an issuer, such as bonds and notes
senses.definitionCN: 代表向发行人提供贷款的工具，如债券与票据
senses.example: The fund shifted from shares into debt securities.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金从股票转向债务证券。
senses.why: One branch of the class is pure borrowing: the holder has lent money and holds a right to interest and repayment.
senses.whyCN: 这一类中的一支是纯粹的借贷：持有人借出了资金，握有收取利息与收回本金的权利。

senses.title: Equity securities
senses.definition: instruments that represent ownership in a company, such as shares
senses.definitionCN: 代表公司所有权的工具，如股票
senses.example: Equity securities carry voting rights and dividend claims.
senses.exampleCN: 权益证券带有表决权与股息主张。
senses.why: The other branch is ownership rather than lending: the holder owns a portion of the company and shares in its fortunes.
senses.whyCN: 另一支是所有权而非借贷：持有人拥有公司的一部分，并与其命运与共。

senses.title: Government securities
senses.definition: debt instruments issued by a government or its agencies
senses.definitionCN: 由政府或其机构发行的债务工具
senses.example: During the crisis investors rushed into government securities.
senses.exampleCN: 危机期间投资者涌向政府证券。
senses.why: The class is narrowed by the issuer: the same instrument is backed by the taxing power of a state rather than by a company.
senses.whyCN: 这一类按发行人收窄：同样的工具由国家征税能力而非公司信用支撑。

senses.title: Certificates of ownership
senses.definition: documents that evidence a right to a share or an asset
senses.definitionCN: 证明对股份或资产享有权利的文件
senses.example: The old certificates were replaced by electronic securities.
senses.exampleCN: 旧式纸质凭证被电子证券取代。
senses.why: Before computers the security was a physical paper that proved the claim, which is the literal root of the financial sense.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机之前，证券就是证明权利的一纸实物，这正是金融义的字面来源。

senses.title: Legal instruments promising payment
senses.definition: legal documents such as promissory notes that bind a party to pay
senses.definitionCN: 本票等把一方约束在付款义务上的法律文书
senses.example: The merchant deposited the securities with his bank.
senses.exampleCN: 商人把那些付款凭证存进了银行。
senses.why: In commercial law a security can be a written promise to pay, so the same plural covers paper that creates a legal obligation.
senses.whyCN: 在商法中，证券也可以是一纸付款承诺，因此同一个复数形式也涵盖产生法律义务的文书。

senses.title: Assets pledged as collateral
senses.definition: assets deposited to guarantee a loan or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 为担保贷款或义务而交存的资产
senses.example: He pledged his securities against the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他用自己的证券为这笔贷款作担保。
senses.why: Here the instrument is used as a shield: the lender holds the security so that a default can be covered by selling it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的工具被当作盾牌：出借人握有担保品，违约时便可出售以弥补损失。

senses.title: The securities industry
senses.definition: the sector of firms that issue, trade or advise on such instruments
senses.definitionCN: 发行、交易或为此类工具提供咨询的行业
senses.example: She spent twenty years working in securities.
senses.exampleCN: 她在证券行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: A mass of instruments and the firms handling them come to be named by the instruments themselves, so the plural stands for an entire trade.
senses.whyCN: 大量工具与处理这些工具的机构，最终以工具本身来命名，于是复数形式代表整个行业。

intro.en: Securities is the plural of security, a word built on Latin cura 'care' with the prefix se- 'without'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: securities 是 security 的复数；security 由拉丁语 cura「忧虑、照料」加前缀 se-「无」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cura meant care, concern or anxiety, and it built words about protecting against trouble.
items.cn: cura 意为照料、忧虑、担心，构成了一批表示防患于未然的词。

items.en: Securitas meant freedom from care or anxiety, a state in which nothing threatens.
items.cn: securitas 意为无忧无虑、免于焦虑，是一种没有威胁的状态。

items.en: Through French the word entered English as a state of safety or certainty, and later as a guarantee against loss.
items.cn: 经法语进入英语后，它先指安全或确定的状态，后来指防损失的保证。

items.en: Tradable claims on debt or ownership came to be called securities because a paper certificate gave the holder assurance of value.
items.cn: 可交易的债权或所有权凭证被称为 securities，因为一纸证书给了持有人关于价值的保障。

items.en: Company and securities law separated the traded instrument from the general idea of safety, fixing the plural as a technical term.
items.cn: 公司法与证券法把可交易工具与一般「安全」概念分开，使复数形式固定为专业术语。

note.en: The first group shares the same root or looks nearly identical; the second group lists other financial instruments and nearby categories.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根或拼写几乎相同；第二组列出其他金融工具与相邻类别。

entries.definition: The singular can mean safety, a guarantee, or one financial instrument; the plural usually means the instruments as a class.
entries.definitionCN: 单数可指安全、保证或一件金融工具；复数通常指作为一类的金融工具。

entries.definition: A guarantee or a person who guarantees another's obligation; it is about backing a promise, not about traded paper.
entries.definitionCN: 担保或为他人义务作保的人；它关乎为承诺作保，而非可交易凭证。

entries.definition: Safe, or to make safe; it keeps the original sense of freedom from danger and lacks the financial plural.
entries.definitionCN: 安全的，或使安全；保留「免于危险」的原义，没有金融上的复数用法。

entries.definition: The process of pooling assets and issuing tradable securities backed by them; it is the action, not the instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 把资产打包并发行以其为支撑的可交易证券的过程；它是动作，不是工具本身。

entries.definition: Shares, treated as a class; equities are one kind of security, not the whole class.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的股份；股票是证券的一种，而非全部。

entries.definition: Debt instruments issued by governments or companies; bonds are another kind of security.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或公司发行的债务工具；债券是证券的另一类。

entries.definition: A general finance term for contracts and documents with monetary value; securities is the narrower legal category.
entries.definitionCN: 金融中对具有货币价值的合约与文书的统称；证券是更窄的法律类别。

entries.definition: Anything bought to produce a return, including property and gold; securities are only the tradable paper part.
entries.definitionCN: 为产生回报而购买的任何东西，包括房产与黄金；证券只是其中可交易的那部分纸面资产。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root for care, real fixed phrases and real related words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语「忧虑」词根、真实固定搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: Security first meant freedom from care; a paper that removes worry about value became a security.
normal.cn: security 本义是免于忧虑；能消除价值担忧的一纸凭证便成了证券。

normal.en: The plural is the class word: stocks, bonds and notes are all securities.
normal.cn: 复数形式是类名词：股票、债券与票据都是证券。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the field: securities market, securities firm, securities law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给这个领域分类：证券市场、证券公司、证券法。

normal.en: Securities can be debt or equity, which are two ways of holding a claim.
normal.cn: 证券可以是债务或权益，这是持有权利的两种方式。

normal.en: Pledged securities act as collateral, so the word returns to its old sense of guarantee.
normal.cn: 用作质押的证券充当担保品，这个词于是回到它古老的「保证」义。

abstract.en: Picture a wallet of stamped papers, each able to turn into money at a shout.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠盖印的纸，每一张都能在一声喊价中变成钱。

abstract.en: Picture the paper dissolving into a number on a screen, still carrying the same claim.
abstract.cn: 想象纸张消融成屏幕上的一串数字，却仍携带同样的权利。

abstract.en: Picture a promise and an ownership share drawn as two different keys to the same lock.
abstract.cn: 想象把承诺与所有权份额画成开同一把锁的两把不同钥匙。

examples.en: The firm was fined for misleading buyers of securities.
examples.cn: 该公司因误导证券买家而被罚款。

examples.en: Foreign investors may purchase government securities freely.
examples.cn: 外国投资者可以自由购买政府证券。

examples.en: She keeps a small part of her savings in securities.
examples.cn: 她把一小部分储蓄放在证券上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安心」的凭证——拿着它，价值有保障，还能在市场上卖掉 → 证券

root: security 出自拉丁语 securitas「无忧、安全」，由 se-「无」加 cura「忧虑、照料」构成；后指能带来价值保障的书面凭证，复数 securities 固定为证券。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide the class by what the paper represents: a tradable claim, a loan, an ownership share, a state-backed debt, a certificate, a promise to pay, a pledge and an entire industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按纸面所代表的东西来划分这一类：可交易权利、贷款、所有权份额、国家背书的债务、凭证、付款承诺、质押品与整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of stamped papers, each convertible into money at a shout.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠盖章的纸，每一张都能在喊价中换成钱。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the plural names tradable financial instruments as a whole.
branches.cn: 类别：复数形式统称可交易的金融工具。

branches.en: LENDING BRANCH: debt securities, including those issued by governments, represent money lent.
branches.cn: 借贷分支：债务证券，包括政府发行的债务证券，代表借出的资金。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP BRANCH: equity securities and share certificates represent a portion owned.
branches.cn: 所有权分支：权益证券与股份凭证代表所拥有的一部分。

branches.en: LEGAL PAPER: a promise to pay or an asset pledged as collateral turns the instrument into a safeguard.
branches.cn: 法律纸面：付款承诺或作为质押品的资产，把工具变成一种保障。

branches.en: TRADE AS A WHOLE: the instruments give their name to the industry that deals in them.
branches.cn: 整体行业：这些工具把名字给了经营它们的行业。

intro.en: Securities belongs to the Latin family of cura, and its derived words move between safety, guarantee and the packaging of assets.
intro.cn: securities 属于拉丁语 cura 一族，其派生词在安全、担保与资产打包之间移动。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura gives security, surety, assure and secure; the prefix se- adds the sense of being free from care.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 衍生出 security、surety、assure 与 secure；前缀 se- 增添「免于忧虑」的意思。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of freedom from worry.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着免于忧虑的意思。

items.meaningCN: 表状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns safe into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「安全」变成一种状态。

items.example: They secured the door before leaving.
The guard provides security at night.

items.meaning: to turn assets into tradable securities
items.meaningCN: 把资产变成可交易证券
items.exampleCN: 放贷机构把房贷资产证券化。

items.meaning: the process of packaging assets as securities
items.meaningCN: 把资产打包为证券的过程
items.example: Securitization spread risk across many buyers.
items.exampleCN: 证券化把风险分散给许多买家。

items.meaningCN: 不安全的，或缺乏信心的
items.exampleCN: 那座旧桥让人缺乏安全感。
工作不稳定让员工担忧。

items.example: His uncle stood surety for the loan.
items.exampleCN: 他叔叔为这笔贷款作担保。

definition_en: a collection of investments or works, or a case for carrying papers
core_image: 一只打开的文件夹，里面夹着分属不同领域的纸张
scene: 投资顾问把客户的资金分散到股票、债券与房产基金，随后摊开文件展示整份组合的年度表现。Her portfolio holds a mix of bonds, shares and property funds.
sceneCN: 这里指「投资组合」，对应第 1 个义项：一个人或机构持有的全部投资；句意为她的组合包含债券、股票与房产基金。画面要点：摊开的文件夹、饼状配置图、年度报表。

pos.zh: 投资组合；作品集；公文包；部长职位；（职责）范围

derivatives.zh: （基金）持股公司；投资组合内公司

senses.title: A collection of investments
senses.definition: the full set of investments held by a person or institution
senses.definitionCN: 个人或机构持有的全部投资
senses.example: The fund rebalanced its portfolio in June.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金在六月调整了投资组合。
senses.why: The word for a case of papers becomes a word for a collection of financial claims: the case holds many sheets, and the investor holds many positions.
senses.whyCN: 原本指装纸的文件夹，转而指一叠金融主张的集合：文件包装许多纸，投资者握有许多头寸。

senses.title: A collection of works
senses.definition: a selection of an artist's or designer's work used to show their ability
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家或设计师用来展示能力的作品选辑
senses.example: She sent her portfolio to three design schools.
senses.exampleCN: 她把作品集寄给了三所设计学校。
senses.why: This keeps the literal case: a folder of samples carried to a meeting, where the collection itself is the argument.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留了字面的文件夹：一叠样张被带到会面现场，合集本身就是论据。

senses.title: A case for carrying papers
senses.definition: a flat case used to carry loose papers, drawings or documents
senses.definitionCN: 用来装散页、图纸或文件的扁平提包
senses.example: He left the meeting with a heavy portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着一只沉重的公文包离开会场。
senses.why: This is the original object: a portable leaf-holder, from which every metaphorical collection sense grows.
senses.whyCN: 这是原本的物件：一只可携带的「装纸器」，所有比喻性的合集义都由它生长出来。

senses.title: A minister's office
senses.definition: the position and duties of a government minister
senses.definitionCN: 政府部长的职位与职务
senses.example: She was given the education portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 她获得了教育部长一职。
senses.why: A minister carries a bundle of responsibilities as if in a case, so the container comes to mean the office held.
senses.whyCN: 部长像提着一只箱子那样承担一束职责，于是容器转而指所担任的职位。

senses.title: A range of responsibilities
senses.definition: the set of duties assigned to one person or team
senses.definitionCN: 分配给一个人或团队的一整套职责
senses.example: Customer service is now part of his portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 客户服务现在属于他的职责范围。
senses.why: The office sense is generalized: any bundle of tasks can be a portfolio because it is a collection held by one owner.
senses.whyCN: 职位义被一般化：任何一束任务都能叫 portfolio，因为它是由一个主体持有的一组合集。

senses.title: An educational portfolio
senses.definition: a curated collection of a student's work used for assessment
senses.definitionCN: 为评估而整理的学生作品合集
senses.example: The course is graded through a portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课通过作品档案来评分。
senses.why: Assessment shifts from a single test to a carried collection, so the folder becomes evidence of learning over time.
senses.whyCN: 评估从单次考试转为一叠随身作品，文件夹于是成了长期学习的证据。

senses.title: A company's product range
senses.definition: the set of products or brands a company offers
senses.definitionCN: 一家公司提供的产品与品牌总体
senses.example: The firm sold its older brands to simplify its portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司出售较老的品牌以精简产品组合。
senses.why: Business treats its offerings as holdings to be balanced, so the investment-collection sense is applied to goods.
senses.whyCN: 企业把所售之物当作需要平衡的持有项，投资合集的义项于是被用到商品上。

senses.title: A collection of projects
senses.definition: a managed set of projects or assets considered together
senses.definitionCN: 被放在一起管理的一批项目或资产
senses.example: The office manages a portfolio of rural road projects.
senses.exampleCN: 该办公室管理着一批乡村道路项目。
senses.why: Any set of undertakings can be balanced like investments, so the word extends from money to work in progress.
senses.whyCN: 任何一束事业都能像投资那样被平衡，于是这个词从资金扩展到进行中的工作。

intro.en: Portfolio is an Italian compound meaning a case for carrying sheets, built from a verb for carrying and a word for a leaf. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portfolio 是意大利语复合词，意为装纸张的提包，由一个表示「携带」的动词与一个表示「纸页」的词构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, and it supplies the first half of the compound and words such as portable and transport.
items.cn: portare 意为携带，提供复合词的前半，也是 portable、transport 等词的来源。

items.en: Folium meant a leaf and also a sheet of paper, which is why a folio is a page and foliage is leafage.
items.cn: folium 意为树叶，也指纸页，所以 folio 指对开页，foliage 指枝叶。

items.en: The Italian compound joined the verb and the noun to name a case in which loose sheets were carried.
items.cn: 意大利语把这个动词与名词合起来，指用来携带散页的提包。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French forms and used it for a minister's case of state papers, then for the office itself.
items.cn: 英语经法语形式借入这个词，先指部长装公文的提包，再指职位本身。

items.en: Investors began to speak of the set of holdings they carried as a portfolio, turning the container into the collection.
items.cn: 投资者开始把所持有的一整套资产称为 portfolio，容器于是变成了合集本身。

note.en: The first group contains words built on the same carrying or leaf parts; the second group names other kinds of collection.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一个「携带」或「纸页」成分上的词；第二组是其他类型的合集。

entries.definition: A leaf of paper or a book made of large sheets; it is the sheet itself, not the case that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 一张纸页或由大张纸装成的书；它是纸页本身，不是装它的提包。

entries.definition: Able to be carried easily; it shares the first element but says nothing about a collection.
entries.definitionCN: 便于携带的；共享第一个成分，但与合集无关。

entries.definition: A harbour or a wine, from Latin portus and portare respectively; only the wine sense shares the carrying verb.
entries.definitionCN: 港口或葡萄酒，分别出自拉丁语的不同词；只有葡萄酒义共享「携带」动词。

entries.definition: A travelling case, and later a word made by blending two words; it is a case, but not the paper-holder.
entries.definitionCN: 旅行箱，后指由两个词混合成的新词；它是箱子，但不是装纸的夹子。

entries.definition: Any set of things gathered together; portfolio is a specialized collection that is managed or assessed.
entries.definitionCN: 任何聚集起来的一批东西；portfolio 是被管理或被评估的专门合集。

entries.definition: The assets a person or fund owns; holdings is more concrete, while portfolio stresses the set as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或基金拥有的资产；holdings 更具体，portfolio 强调整套。

entries.definition: A flat case for carrying documents; it is the everyday object, while portfolio is the older Italian loan for the same item.
entries.definitionCN: 装文件的扁平提包；它是日常物件，portfolio 是同一物件的较早意大利语借词。

entries.definition: A file of papers about one person or case; it is a collection of documents, not of investments or works.
entries.definitionCN: 关于某人或某案的一叠文件；它是文件合集，不是投资或作品合集。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Italian parts meaning carry and leaf, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的意大利语成分「携带」与「纸页」、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Portare means carry and folium means leaf or sheet, so a portfolio is a sheet-carrier.
normal.cn: 前一半意为携带，后一半意为纸页，所以 portfolio 就是装纸页的器物。

normal.en: The case came first, the collection came later: investors now carry positions instead of papers.
normal.cn: 先有器物，后有合集：投资者如今携带的是头寸而不是纸页。

normal.en: A minister's portfolio is a bundle of duties carried as if in a case.
normal.cn: 部长的 portfolio 是一束像装在箱子里那样随身承担的职责。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the finance sense: investment portfolio, portfolio manager, loan portfolio.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金融义：投资组合、组合经理、贷款组合。

normal.en: Art and education keep the older folder sense: an art portfolio and an assessment portfolio.
normal.cn: 艺术与教育保留了较早的文件夹义：作品集与学习档案。

abstract.en: Picture an open case of sheets, each sheet a different kind of claim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只打开的文件箱，每张纸都是不同种类的主张。

abstract.en: Picture the case shrinking until it is only the set of claims, no paper at all.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子不断缩小，最后只剩下那套主张，连纸也没有了。

abstract.en: Picture the same shape reappearing as a range of products or a bundle of duties.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个形状再次出现，成为一组产品或一束职责。

examples.en: A diversified portfolio can survive a single bad year.
examples.cn: 分散的投资组合能挺过单个糟糕年份。

examples.en: The designer revised her portfolio before the interview.
examples.cn: 设计师在面试前修改了作品集。

examples.en: He carried a leather portfolio under his arm.
examples.cn: 他腋下夹着一只皮制公文包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「随身携带的一叠纸」——把各种资产像纸页一样装进同一只夹子 → 投资组合

root: 意大利语 portafoglio「装纸的提包」，由 portare「携带」（拉丁语 portare）与 foglio「纸页」（拉丁语 folium）构成；后由「携带的文件」引申为一人所持的一整套投资、作品或职责。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from a case of sheets and end with any managed collection: investments, artworks, duties, student work, products and projects.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一只装纸的提包出发，最终落在任何被管理的合集：投资、作品、职责、学生作业、产品与项目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open case of loose sheets, each sheet a different claim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只打开的文件箱，散页各代表不同的主张。

branches.en: SET OF CLAIMS: the carried papers become a set of financial positions watched as one.
branches.cn: 一套主张：随身携带的纸变成一整套被整体关注的投资头寸。

branches.en: SET OF WORKS AND GOODS: art samples and product ranges are held together for display or balance.
branches.cn: 作品与商品合集：艺术样张与产品线被放在一起展示或平衡。

branches.en: THE CASE ITSELF: the literal object that every other sense borrows from.
branches.cn: 器物本身：其他所有义项都借用这个字面物件。

branches.en: OFFICE AND DUTIES: a bundle of state papers becomes the minister's office, then any range of responsibilities.
branches.cn: 职位与职责：一束公文先变成部长职位，再泛指任何职责范围。

branches.en: ASSESSED AND MANAGED SETS: a student's file and a project group are collections run as a whole.
branches.cn: 被评估与管理的合集：学生学习档案与项目群都是作为整体运营的合集。

intro.en: Portfolio is a borrowed Italian compound, and its parts remain visible in words about carrying and about sheets of paper.
intro.cn: portfolio 是借入的意大利语复合词，其组成部分在表示「携带」与「纸页」的词里仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: The two Latin sources are portare for carrying and folium for a leaf or sheet; both produced families of English words.
latinIntro.cn: 两个拉丁来源分别是表示携带的 portare 与表示树叶或纸页的 folium，两者都产生了英语词族。

The two portfolios overlap in energy.
items.exampleCN: 这两个组合在能源上重叠。

items.example: The bank ran a portfolio-wide review.

items.example: The portfolio manager shifted into bonds.

items.meaning: grading based on a collected body of work

items.example: The poem fills a single folio.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗占满一页对开纸。

items.meaningCN: 携带，如运输一词中的成分

items.meaning: a page or leaf in compounds
items.meaningCN: 复合词中表示纸页的成分
items.example: The suffix names a kind of page.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分表示某类纸页。
