definition_zh: 多样化；分散投资；业务多元化
definition_en: the process of adding variety, especially by spreading investments or activities
core_image: 一只篮子里的鸡蛋被分装到许多只篮子，每只篮子走向不同的方向
scene: 理财顾问把客户的资金分到不同行业与地区，以避免单一市场崩盘带来的冲击。Diversification reduced the fund's loss when one sector collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里指「分散投资」，对应第 2 个义项：把资金分散到不同资产以降低风险；句意为一个行业崩盘时，分散化降低了基金的损失。画面要点：多只篮子、行业标签、下跌曲线。

pos.zh: 多样化；分散化；分散投资；业务多元化

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次分散过程）

derivatives.zh: 分散风险者；多元化经营者

senses.title: The general process of adding variety
senses.definition: the act of making something include a wider range of types
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物包含更广泛类型的行为
senses.example: Diversification of the curriculum widened student choice.
senses.exampleCN: 课程多样化扩大了学生的选择。
senses.why: The noun names the act of turning one kind into many, the most general reading of the verb behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指把一种变成多种的动作，是背后动词最一般的读法。

senses.title: Spreading investments
senses.definition: the practice of spreading money across assets so that one failure does not sink the whole
senses.definitionCN: 把资金分散到不同资产，使单一失败不至于拖垮整体
senses.example: Diversification cannot remove risk, only redistribute it.
senses.exampleCN: 分散投资不能消除风险，只能重新分配风险。
senses.why: In finance the many kinds are many holdings; the purpose is not variety for its own sake but spreading the chance of loss.
senses.whyCN: 在金融中，多种类就是多项持有；目的不是为多样而多样，而是分散损失的可能性。

senses.title: Entering new lines of business
senses.definition: a company's expansion into products or markets different from its original one
senses.definitionCN: 公司扩展到与原业务不同的产品或市场
senses.example: Diversification into software saved the publisher.
senses.exampleCN: 向软件业务多元化拯救了这家出版商。
senses.why: A firm with one product is a basket with one egg, so the word describes adding other baskets of revenue.
senses.whyCN: 只有一种产品的公司就像只放一枚鸡蛋的篮子，这个词因此指增添其他收入篮子。

senses.title: Spreading across regions
senses.definition: the expansion of activity into different countries or regions
senses.definitionCN: 把活动扩展到不同国家或地区
senses.example: Geographic diversification protected sales during the home slowdown.
senses.exampleCN: 地域分散化在本国放缓期间保住了销售。
senses.why: The many kinds here are many places: a collapse in one region is offset by activity elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这里的多种类是多个地方：一个地区的崩塌可由别处的活动来抵消。

senses.title: Crop diversification
senses.definition: the practice of growing several crops instead of relying on one
senses.definitionCN: 种植多种作物而不是依赖单一作物的做法
senses.example: Crop diversification improved the soil and the farmer's income.
senses.exampleCN: 作物多样化改善了土壤，也提高了农民收入。
senses.why: Agriculture applies the financial logic to the field: several crops hedge against weather and price swings.
senses.whyCN: 农业把金融逻辑搬到田里：几种作物共同对冲天气与价格波动。

senses.title: Economic diversification
senses.definition: the broadening of a regional or national economy beyond one industry
senses.definitionCN: 把地区或国家经济扩展到单一产业之外
senses.example: Oil revenue funded the country's economic diversification.
senses.exampleCN: 石油收入资助了这个国家的经济多元化。
senses.why: A whole economy can be a single basket, so the word scales up from a firm to a state.
senses.whyCN: 整个经济体也可以是一只单一的篮子，于是这个词从公司放大到国家。

senses.title: Biological diversification
senses.definition: the increase of variety among species or genes over time
senses.definitionCN: 物种或基因随时间增加多样性
senses.example: Island isolation drove rapid diversification of the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 岛屿隔离推动了这些鸟类的快速分化。
senses.why: Biology uses the same shape without human choice: one ancestral form branches into many forms.
senses.whyCN: 生物学使用同样的形状，却没有人为选择：一个祖型分化为许多类型。

senses.title: The resulting mixed state
senses.titleCN: 分散之后形成的混合状态
senses.definition: the condition of being made up of varied parts rather than one
senses.definitionCN: 由多种成分而非单一成分构成的状态
senses.example: The portfolio's diversification made its returns smoother.
senses.exampleCN: 这个组合的分散状态使其回报更平稳。
senses.why: The word can name not only the act but the result: a whole that is now visibly made of many parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅能指动作，也能指结果：一个如今明显由许多部分构成的整体。

intro.en: Diversification is an English noun built on Latin roots meaning to turn apart and to make. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: diversification 是英语名词，建立在表示「转向别处」与「制造」的拉丁词根上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, and it underlies divertere, convertere and a large family of English words about turning.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动，是 divertere、convertere 以及一大批表示「转」的英语词的底层。

items.en: Diversus meant turned in different directions, hence various or separate, the source of diverse and diversity.
items.cn: diversus 意为被转向不同方向，因此指多样或分开，是 diverse 与 diversity 的来源。

items.en: The verb joined diversus with facere 'to make', literally to make things turn apart, that is, to make them varied.
items.cn: 这个动词把 diversus 与 facere「制造」结合，字面是使事物转向不同方向，也就是使之多样。

items.en: French carried the verb into ordinary use, and English borrowed the verb in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词带入日常使用，英语在十七世纪借入了该动词。

items.en: The noun ending -ification names the process of making, so diversification is literally the making of variety.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ification 表示「使……的过程」，所以 diversification 字面上就是「使多样」。

items.en: Twentieth-century finance and management gave the noun its specialized readings: spreading holdings, markets and products.
items.cn: 二十世纪的金融与管理学赋予这个名词专门含义：分散持有、市场与产品。

note.en: The first group is built from the same turning root; the second group names the result or a neighboring strategy.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「转」的词根上；第二组指结果或相邻策略。

entries.definition: The state of having many different kinds; diversification is the act of producing that state.
entries.definitionCN: 具有许多不同种类的状态；diversification 是产生这种状态的动作。

entries.definition: Varied or different; it describes the parts, while diversification names the change that creates them.
entries.definitionCN: 多样的、不同的；它描述各个部分，而 diversification 指创造这些部分的变化。

entries.definition: To turn something aside or to entertain; it shares the turning image but has no sense of adding variety.
entries.definitionCN: 使转向一旁，或使娱乐；共享「转」的意象，但没有增加多样的意思。

entries.definition: A change of route or an amusement; it turns one thing away rather than multiplying kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 改道或消遣；它是把一样东西转开，而不是增加种类。

entries.definition: Distributing something over a wider area; in finance it is the practical effect of diversification.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物分布到更广的范围；在金融中它是分散化的实际效果。

entries.definition: Making a range wider; it stresses extent, while diversification stresses the addition of different types.
entries.definitionCN: 使范围更宽；强调广度，而分散化强调加入不同类型。

entries.definition: Growth in size or reach; expansion can stay in one line, while diversification must cross into another.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或范围的扩大；扩张可以停留在同一业务线，而多元化必须跨到另一条。

entries.definition: Taking an offsetting position to reduce risk; hedging is one reason to diversify, not the same action.
entries.definitionCN: 建立对冲头寸以降低风险；对冲是分散化的一个理由，而不是同一动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real turning root, the real making suffix and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「转动」词根、真实的「制造」后缀与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The first half means turned apart, the second half means making, so the word is making things turn apart.
normal.cn: 前半意为转向不同方向，后半意为制造，所以这个词就是使事物分向多处。

normal.en: Finance applies it to eggs and baskets: many holdings instead of one.
normal.cn: 金融把它用到鸡蛋与篮子上：多项持有而不是只有一项。

normal.en: Business applies it to products and regions; agriculture applies it to crops.
normal.cn: 企业把它用到产品与地区；农业把它用到作物。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: portfolio, product, geographic, economic, crop.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出尺度：组合、产品、地域、经济、作物。

normal.en: Diversity is the state; diversification is the act that produces it.
normal.cn: diversity 是状态，diversification 是产生该状态的动作。

abstract.en: Picture one egg in one basket, then the same egg copied into many baskets walking in different directions.
abstract.cn: 想象一只篮子里放一枚鸡蛋，随后同一枚蛋被分装到许多只走向不同方向的篮子。

abstract.en: Picture a single road splitting into many roads, so no closure can stop all travel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路分成许多条，任何一处封闭都无法阻断全部通行。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree branching outward, the same shape as a portfolio spreading outward.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树向外分枝，与投资组合向外分散是同一个形状。

examples.en: Diversification is the first rule taught to new investors.
examples.cn: 分散投资是教给新投资者的第一条规则。

examples.en: The region's diversification away from mining took a decade.
examples.cn: 该地区摆脱对矿业的依赖、走向多元化花了十年。

examples.en: Genetic diversification helps a species survive a new disease.
examples.cn: 遗传多样化帮助物种挺过新的疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分成许多样」——把鸡蛋分到许多篮子里 → 分散投资、多样化

root: 由拉丁语 diversus「转向不同方向的、多样的」与 facere「制造」结合，经法语进入英语；名词后缀表示「使……的过程」，故字面义为「使多样」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general act of adding variety to its financial, business, regional, agricultural, economic and biological applications, and finally to the mixed state it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般的「增加多样」动作，转到金融、企业、地域、农业、经济与生物上的应用，最后落在它所产生的混合状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eggs from one basket distributed among many baskets heading in different directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只篮子里的鸡蛋被分到许多只走向不同方向的篮子。

branches.en: GENERAL ACT: one kind is deliberately turned into many kinds.
branches.cn: 一般动作：一种被有意变成多种。

branches.en: INVESTMENT AND RESULT: money is spread across assets, and the portfolio ends up visibly mixed.
branches.cn: 投资与结果：资金分散到各种资产，组合最终呈现为可见的混合体。

branches.en: BUSINESS AND PLACE: a firm adds new lines and new regions so no single market decides its fate.
branches.cn: 企业与地点：公司增添新业务线与新地区，使单一市场无法决定其命运。

branches.en: FIELD AND STATE: crops and whole economies are diversified for the same hedge against one failure.
branches.cn: 田地与国家：作物与整个经济体为同样的「防单一失败」而对冲。

branches.en: NATURAL BRANCHING: evolution produces variety without a human planner.
branches.cn: 自然分枝：演化在没有人类规划者的情况下产生多样性。

intro.en: Diversification is built from Latin pieces that still work productively in English: a turning root, a making suffix and a process ending.
intro.cn: diversification 由仍在英语中能产的拉丁成分构成：一个「转」的词根、一个「制造」的后缀与一个表过程的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere 'to turn' gives divert, convert and reverse; diversus adds the idea of turning apart, and facere supplies the making.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere「转」衍生 divert、convert 与 reverse；diversus 增添「转向别处」的意思，facere 提供「制造」。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在转变与反转等词里。

definition_en: to make something more varied, or to spread money or activity across different areas
core_image: 一只手把同一种东西撒向好几块不同的田地
scene: 一家只卖一种农产品的家族企业决定把业务扩展到食品加工与乡村旅店。The family firm decided to diversify into food processing and rural tourism.
sceneCN: 这里指「把业务扩展到新的领域」，对应第 3 个义项：企业进入与原业务不同的产品线；句意为这家家族企业决定向食品加工与乡村旅游业多元化。画面要点：农田、加工车间、旅店招牌。

pos.zh: 使多样化；分散（投资）；开展多元化业务；增加（作物、来源等的）种类

derivatives.zh: 分散风险者；多元化经营者

senses.title: To make more varied
senses.definition: to introduce a wider range of types into something
senses.definitionCN: 把更广泛的类型引入某事物
senses.example: The school diversified its reading list.
senses.exampleCN: 学校使阅读书单更加多样。
senses.why: The verb is the general action behind the noun: one line of things is turned into several lines.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是名词背后的一般动作：一条线上的一类东西被转成好几条线。

senses.title: To spread investments
senses.definition: to put money into several assets instead of one
senses.definitionCN: 把钱投入多项资产而不是只投一项
senses.example: Retirees should diversify before markets turn.
senses.exampleCN: 退休者应在市场转向之前先分散投资。
senses.why: Finance turns the general act into risk management: many assets mean many chances instead of one.
senses.whyCN: 金融把这个一般动作变成风险管理：多项资产意味着多个机会而不是一个。

senses.title: To enter new lines of business
senses.definition: for a company, to expand into products or services beyond its original line
senses.definitionCN: 企业扩展到原业务之外的产品或服务
senses.example: The chain diversified into coffee shops.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁企业扩展到咖啡店业务。
senses.why: A firm that adds a second line is literally adding kinds to its basket of revenue.
senses.whyCN: 增添第二条业务线的公司，实际上是在其收入篮子里加上新的种类。

senses.title: To vary products or markets
senses.definition: to change the mix of goods sold or the markets served
senses.definitionCN: 改变所售商品或所服务市场的组合
senses.example: The exporter diversified its markets across Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 这家出口商在亚洲各地分散市场。
senses.why: Here the added kinds are goods and destinations, so the verb shifts from entering a line to changing the mix.
senses.whyCN: 这里增添的种类是商品与目的地，动词因此从「进入一条线」转为「改变组合」。

senses.title: To broaden an economy
senses.definition: to reduce a region's dependence on one industry
senses.definitionCN: 降低一个地区对单一产业的依赖
senses.example: The province diversified away from timber.
senses.exampleCN: 该省从木材业转向多元化。
senses.why: The verb scales a company strategy up to a whole region: one industry is replaced by several.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把企业策略放大到整个地区：一个产业被好几个产业取代。

senses.title: To increase genetic variety
senses.definition: to widen the range of genes in a population or crop
senses.definitionCN: 扩大种群或作物的基因范围
senses.example: Plant breeders diversify wheat to resist disease.
senses.exampleCN: 育种者使小麦多样化以抗病。
senses.why: Breeding uses the same act without markets: more kinds in the gene pool mean fewer total failures.
senses.whyCN: 育种在没有市场的情况下使用同一动作：基因库里种类更多，整体失败就更少。

senses.title: To expand one's range of activity
senses.definition: for a person or group, to take on new kinds of work or interest
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体承担新的工作或兴趣种类
senses.example: She diversified her practice to include family law.
senses.exampleCN: 她扩展业务范围，纳入了家庭法。
senses.why: A career or practice can be a portfolio of activities, so the verb applies to a person's bundle of work.
senses.whyCN: 职业或业务可以是一组活动，因此这个动词也能用于一个人的工作束。

senses.title: To grow several crops
senses.definition: to replace a single crop with several on the same farm
senses.definitionCN: 在同一农场上以多种作物取代单一作物
senses.example: The cooperative diversified into fruit and nuts.
senses.exampleCN: 合作社多样化种植水果与坚果。
senses.why: The field is the simplest basket: several crops spread the risk of weather and price.
senses.whyCN: 田地是最简单的篮子：几种作物分散天气与价格风险。

senses.title: To change the mix of sources
senses.definition: to add different sources of supply or energy
senses.definitionCN: 增加不同的供应或能源来源
senses.example: The grid diversified into wind and solar power.
senses.exampleCN: 电网向风能与太阳能多元化。
senses.why: Sources are supplies, so the same verb says: do not depend on one well, one pipe or one country.
senses.whyCN: 来源就是供应，所以同一个动词表达：不要只依赖一口井、一条管道或一个国家。

intro.en: Diversify is an English verb formed from Latin diversus 'turned apart' and facere 'to make'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: diversify 是英语动词，由拉丁语 diversus「转向别处」与 facere「制造」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn; its participle supplied the idea of being turned in another direction.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动；它的分词形式提供了「被转向另一方向」的意思。

items.en: Diversus meant turned apart or various, the direct ancestor of diverse and diversity.
items.cn: diversus 意为被转开或多样的，是 diverse 与 diversity 的直接祖先。

items.en: Diversificare joined that adjective with facere 'to make' to mean to make different or varied.
items.cn: diversificare 把这个形容词与 facere「制造」结合，意为使不同、使多样。

items.en: French used the verb in ordinary speech, and English borrowed it in the seventeenth century as diversify.
items.cn: 法语在日常语言中使用这个动词，英语在十七世纪以 diversify 的形式借入。

items.en: Modern finance applied the verb to holdings and modern industry applied it to products, markets and regions.
items.cn: 现代金融把这个动词用于持有资产，现代产业则把它用于产品、市场与地区。

note.en: The first group is built on the same turning root and is often confused with it; the second group contains verbs of widening or varying.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「转」的词根上，常被混淆；第二组是表示扩大或变化的动词。

entries.definition: A change of route or an entertainment; it turns one thing away rather than adding kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 改道或消遣；它把一样东西转开，而不是增加种类。

entries.definition: The state of being varied; it is the result, while diversify is the action that creates it.
entries.definitionCN: 多样的状态；它是结果，而 diversify 是创造它的动作。

entries.definition: Of many different kinds; it describes a set, not the process of changing it.
entries.definitionCN: 许多不同种类的；它描述一个集合，而不是改变它的过程。

entries.definition: To change the course of something; it does not mean to multiply its kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 改变某物的方向；不表示增加其种类。

entries.definition: To make or become different over time; vary stresses change, diversify stresses adding kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 使或变得不同；vary 强调变化，diversify 强调增加种类。

entries.definition: To make wider in scope; it stresses extent rather than the number of kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 使范围更宽；强调广度而非种类的数量。

entries.definition: To grow in size or reach; expansion may stay within one business, while diversification must cross boundaries.
entries.definitionCN: 在规模或范围上增长；扩张可以在同一业务内，而多元化必须跨界。

entries.definition: To distribute over an area; in finance it describes the physical result of diversifying.
entries.definitionCN: 分布到一片区域；在金融中描述分散化的实际结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The word is make plus turned apart: to diversify is to make things head in different directions.
normal.cn: 这个词是「制造」加「转向别处」：多元化就是让事物朝不同方向走。

normal.en: Money diversifies into assets, a firm into products, a region into industries, a farm into crops.
normal.cn: 资金分散到资产，企业扩展到产品，地区扩展到产业，农场扩展到作物。

normal.en: The fixed phrase diversify into marks the new field being entered.
normal.cn: 表示「扩展到某一领域」的固定说法标出正在进入的新领域。

normal.en: Diversify away from marks the old dependence being reduced.
normal.cn: 表示「从某一领域转向别处」的说法标出正在减少的旧依赖。

normal.en: The noun diversification and the adjective diversified come from this verb, not the other way round.
normal.cn: 名词 diversification 与形容词 diversified 都从这个动词而来，而不是反过来。

abstract.en: Picture one hand scattering the same seed over several fields, so no single storm can take the whole harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把同一种种子撒向好几块田，任何一场风暴都拿不走全部收成。

abstract.en: Picture a single stream split into several channels, each able to supply water if another dries.
abstract.cn: 想象一条水流分成几道渠，任何一条干了，其余仍能供水。

abstract.en: Picture a person's work splitting into several skills, so one closed door does not end the career.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人的工作分成几项技能，一扇门关上并不终结整个职业。

examples.en: Farmers were advised to diversify their crops after the drought.
examples.cn: 干旱之后，农民被建议使作物多样化。

examples.en: The fund diversifies across regions and industries.
examples.cn: 该基金在地域与行业上分散投资。

examples.en: The city hopes to diversify away from tourism.
examples.cn: 这座城市希望摆脱对旅游业的依赖而走向多元化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「使分成许多样」——把投资、产品、作物都分成好几路 → 多元化

root: 由拉丁语 diversus「转向别处的、多样的」与 facere「制造」构成，经法语进入英语；核心动作是使一类事物变成多类。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses apply one act to different objects: reading lists, portfolios, business lines, markets, regional economies, genes, careers, crops and energy sources.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把同一个动作用到不同对象上：书单、投资组合、业务线、市场、地区经济、基因、职业、作物与能源来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand scattering the same seed across several fields.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把同一种种子撒向好几块田。

branches.en: GENERAL ACTION: a single range is deliberately widened into several kinds.
branches.cn: 一般动作：单一范围被有意拓宽成好几种。

branches.en: FINANCIAL ACTION: money is placed in many assets instead of one.
branches.cn: 金融动作：资金被放进多项资产而不是只有一项。

branches.en: NEW WORK: a firm adds business lines and a person adds kinds of practice.
branches.cn: 新工作：公司增添业务线，个人增添业务种类。

branches.en: WIDENING MIX: products, regional industries and supply sources are all re-mixed.
branches.cn: 拓宽组合：产品、地区产业与供应来源都被重新调配。

branches.en: NATURAL AND FIELD VARIETY: genes and crops are varied so one disease cannot take everything.
branches.cn: 自然与田地的多样：基因与作物被多样化，使一种病害拿不走全部。

intro.cn: diversify 是一个结构清楚的拉丁来源动词：一个「转」的词根、一个「制造」的后缀，以及一族相关名词与形容词。

definition_en: a share of profit paid to shareholders, or a number to be divided
core_image: 一只钱袋被分成几小袋，递给持有股份的人
scene: 公司年报公布后，董事会决定把更多利润以现金分给持股人。The board raised the dividend after a strong year.
sceneCN: 这里指「分给股东的利润」，对应第 1 个义项：公司从利润中按股份支付给股东的款项；句意为业绩强劲的一年后，董事会提高了股息。画面要点：年报、钱袋、股东名单。

pos.zh: 股息；红利；被除数；回报；保单红利

senses.title: A share of profit paid to shareholders
senses.definition: a part of a company's profit distributed to its shareholders
senses.definitionCN: 公司利润中分给股东的一部分
senses.example: The company pays a dividend twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每年派发两次股息。
senses.why: The word literally means that which is to be divided: profit is cut into portions and one portion goes to each share.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上指「应当被分掉的东西」：利润被切成几份，每份股份得一份。

senses.title: An interim or final payment
senses.titleCN: 期中或期末派发的股息
senses.definition: a dividend paid at a scheduled point in the financial year
senses.definitionCN: 在财年某个既定节点支付的股息
senses.example: The interim dividend rose to eight cents.
senses.exampleCN: 期中股息升至八分。
senses.why: The same share of profit is named by its timing, since a payment can be made halfway through the year or at its close.
senses.whyCN: 同一份利润按支付时点得名，因为款项可以在年中或年末支付。

senses.title: A benefit from an action
senses.definition: an advantage or return that results from effort or investment
senses.definitionCN: 由努力或投入产生的益处或回报
senses.example: The training paid dividends in fewer accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项培训在减少事故上带来了回报。
senses.why: Profit is abstracted from money to any good result, so an effort can be said to pay dividends even without shares.
senses.whyCN: 利润从金钱抽象为任何好结果，所以即使没有股份，一项努力也能说带来回报。

senses.title: A number to be divided
senses.definition: the number that is divided by another in arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 算术中被另一个数除的数
senses.example: In twelve divided by three, twelve is the dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 在十二除以三中，十二是被除数。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense: the quantity that is cut up by division, before finance borrowed the name.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面义：被除法切分的数量，金融后来借用了这个名字。

senses.title: An insurance policy dividend
senses.definition: a share of surplus returned to holders of certain insurance policies
senses.definitionCN: 某些保险保单持有人分得的盈余份额
senses.example: The mutual insurer returned a dividend to policyholders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家互助保险公司向保单持有人返还了红利。
senses.why: An insurer's surplus is divided among the people who funded it, so the profit-share sense moves from shares to policies.
senses.whyCN: 保险公司的盈余在出资人之间分配，利润份额义于是从股份转到保单。

senses.title: A cooperative patronage dividend
senses.titleCN: 合作社按交易量分配的盈余
senses.definition: a share of a cooperative's surplus returned according to members' trade
senses.definitionCN: 合作社按成员交易额返还的盈余份额
senses.example: The farmers' cooperative paid a patronage dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 农民合作社支付了按交易额计算的盈余。
senses.why: Cooperative members are owners and customers at once, so surplus is divided by how much each used the business.
senses.whyCN: 合作社成员同时是所有者与顾客，所以盈余按各人使用企业的多少来分。

senses.title: A dividend paid in shares
senses.definition: a distribution made by issuing additional shares instead of cash
senses.definitionCN: 通过增发股份而非现金进行的分配
senses.example: The company chose a stock dividend to keep cash.
senses.exampleCN: 公司选择股票股利以保留现金。
senses.why: The portion is still divided out, but the portion consists of new shares rather than money.
senses.whyCN: 分出去的仍然是份额，只是这一份由新股份而不是现金构成。

senses.title: A dividend paid in cash
senses.definition: a distribution paid directly in money
senses.definitionCN: 直接以金钱支付的分配
senses.example: Investors prefer a steady cash dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者偏好稳定的现金股息。
senses.why: This is the plainest financial reading: profit is divided and the holder receives money rather than paper.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的金融读法：利润被分开，持有人收到的是钱而不是纸。

intro.en: Dividend comes from a Latin gerundive meaning that which is to be divided; the arithmetic sense is older than the financial one. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dividend 出自拉丁语动形词，意为「应当被分掉的东西」；算术义早于金融义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dividere meant to force apart, cleave or distribute; it is generally analysed as dis- 'apart' plus a second element meaning to separate, though the deeper origin of that element is source uncertain.
items.cn: dividere 意为分开、劈开、分配；一般分析为 dis-「分开」加一个表示「分离」的成分，但该成分更深的来源不确定。

items.en: The gerundive dividendum meant that which is to be divided, a form used in arithmetic and in sharing out amounts.
items.cn: 动形词 dividendum 意为「应当被分掉的东西」，用于算术与分配数额。

items.en: English arithmetic books used dividend for the number to be divided, the sense that still survives in mathematics.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语算术书用 dividend 指被除数，这一义项至今留在数学中。

items.en: Joint-stock companies began to divide surplus profit among shareholders and called each portion a dividend.
items.cn: 合股公司开始把剩余利润分给股东，并把每一份称为 dividend。

items.en: Insurance, cooperatives and stock-based payments extended the word to policyholders, members and shares issued instead of cash.
items.cn: 保险、合作社与以股代现的支付方式，把这个词扩展到保单持有人、合作社成员与增发股份。

note.en: The first group is built on the same dividing root and is easily confused; the second group names other kinds of payment or return.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「分开」的词根上，容易混淆；第二组是其他类型的支付或回报。

entries.definition: The number by which another is divided; the dividend is above the line, the divisor below it.
entries.definitionCN: 用来除另一个数的数；被除数在除号上方，除数在下方。

entries.definition: The act or operation of dividing; it is the process, while a dividend is one of the quantities involved.
entries.definitionCN: 划分或除的动作；它是过程，而 dividend 是参与其中的一个量。

entries.definition: To separate or share out; the verb names the action that produces a dividend.
entries.definitionCN: 分开或分配；动词表示产生股息或被除数的动作。

entries.definition: A single person, literally one that cannot be divided; it shares the root but has no sense of a portion paid out.
entries.definitionCN: 单个的人，字面是「不可再分者」；共享词根，但没有分出份额的意思。

entries.definition: A sum of money paid out, from insurance, gambling or a company; it is broader than dividend.
entries.definitionCN: 从保险、博彩或公司付出的款项；比股息更宽泛。

entries.definition: The formal sharing out of money or assets; a dividend is one kind of distribution.
entries.definitionCN: 对金钱或资产的正式分配；股息是分配的一种。

entries.definition: An extra payment, often discretionary; a dividend follows ownership, while a bonus often follows performance.
entries.definitionCN: 额外支付的款项，常出于酌情；股息跟随所有权，奖金常跟随业绩。

entries.definition: The total gain from an investment, including interest and price change; a dividend is only one part of a return.
entries.definitionCN: 投资的总收益，包括利息与价格变化；股息只是回报的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin meaning that which is to be divided, real fixed phrases and real arithmetic relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语「应当被分掉者」、真实固定搭配与真实算术同族词。

normal.en: The word is the thing to be divided, which explains both the arithmetic and the financial senses.
normal.cn: 这个词就是「要被分掉的东西」，这同时解释了算术义与金融义。

normal.en: Profit is cut into portions, and each share receives one portion.
normal.cn: 利润被切成几份，每一股得到其中一份。

normal.en: Insurance surplus and cooperative surplus are divided the same way among the people who funded them.
normal.cn: 保险盈余与合作社盈余也按同样方式在出资人之间分配。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the finance sense: dividend yield, cash dividend, stock dividend.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金融义：股息收益率、现金股息、股票股利。

normal.en: The phrase pay dividends keeps the metaphor alive: effort is an investment that can return a portion.
normal.cn: 「产生回报」这一说法保留了比喻：努力是一项能返回一份的投资。

abstract.en: Picture a money bag opened and its contents split into small bags for the people who own the company.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱袋被打开，里面的钱分成小袋，交给拥有公司的人。

abstract.en: Picture the same splitting action drawn as a number above a line, waiting to be divided.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个分配动作画成横线上方的一个数，等待被除。

abstract.en: Picture a seed of effort later opening into several small bags of benefit.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒努力的种子后来裂开成几小袋好处。

examples.en: Shareholders approved the higher dividend at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 股东们在年度会议上批准了更高的股息。

examples.en: Patience with the new process paid dividends within a year.
examples.cn: 对新流程的耐心在一年内带来了回报。

examples.en: In the expression forty divided by eight, forty is the dividend.
examples.cn: 在四十除以八这个算式中，四十是被除数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「利润被分成小份」——每一股拿一份 → 股息；算式里被除的那个数 → 被除数

root: 拉丁语 dividere「分开、分配」的动形词 dividendum「应当被分掉的东西」；先用于算术的被除数，十七世纪起用于分给股东的利润份额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all depend on division: a profit is cut into portions, a scheduled payment is named by its timing, the benefit spreads beyond money, and arithmetic keeps the oldest literal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都依赖「分开」：利润被切成几份，按支付时点得名，好处超出金钱，而算术保留了最古老的字面义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a money bag split into small bags for the people who own the company.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只钱袋被分成小袋，交给拥有公司的人。

branches.en: CORE SHARE: profit is divided, and one portion follows each share.
branches.cn: 核心份额：利润被分开，每一股跟随一份。

branches.en: FORMS OF PAYMENT: the same portion can be interim or final, paid in cash or issued as shares.
branches.cn: 支付形式：同一份可以是期中或期末，以现金支付或以股份发放。

branches.en: BENEFIT: the divided portion becomes any good result that effort returns.
branches.cn: 好处：被分出的份额变成努力返回的任何好结果。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: the quantity that is to be divided keeps the oldest literal meaning.
branches.cn: 算术：应当被除的那个量保留了最古老的字面义。

branches.en: OTHER SURPLUS: insurers and cooperatives divide surplus among policyholders and members.
branches.cn: 其他盈余：保险公司与合作社在保单持有人与成员之间分配盈余。

intro.en: Dividend belongs to the Latin family of dividere, whose pieces still appear in English words about separation and arithmetic.
intro.cn: dividend 属于拉丁语 dividere 一族，其成分仍出现在表示分离与算术的英语词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin dividere 'to divide' gives divide, division, divisor and individual, literally one who cannot be divided.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dividere「分开」衍生 divide、division、divisor 与 individual，后者字面是「不可再分者」。

items.example: The stem appears in divide and division.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在划分与除法等词里。

items.meaning: that which is to be done
items.meaningCN: 应当被做的（动形词词尾）
items.example: The ending marks something due to be acted on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标示应当被处理的对象。

items.meaning: the act of dividing, or a part formed by it
items.meaningCN: 划分动作，或由此形成的部分
items.example: The division of labour raised output.

items.meaning: a portion of profit, or a number to be divided
items.example: The dividend was paid in June.

items.meaning: the number by which one divides
items.example: Eight is the divisor in this sum.
items.exampleCN: 在这个算式里八是除数。
这项提案被证明会造成分歧。

latinEntries.meaning: a single person, literally not divisible
latinEntries.meaningCN: 个人，字面为不可再分者

latinEntries.meaning: to divide again into smaller parts
the quantity or profit to be divided

definition_zh: 产出；产量；收益率；屈服；让路；交出；塌陷；承认；反应产率
definition_en: to produce something, to give way, or the amount produced or earned
core_image: 一株果树把果子交出来，树身也被重量压得弯下
scene: 果园里，工人把刚摘下的苹果装箱过秤，这一季的收成足够供应整个村子。The orchard yields enough apples to supply the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里指「产出、出产」，对应第 1 个义项：土地或植物生产出某物；句意为这座果园出产的苹果足以供应整个村子。画面要点：果树、果筐、过秤的工人。

pos.zh: 产出；产生；屈服；让路；交出；塌陷；承认
产量；收成；收益率；产率

derivatives.zh: 顺从的；出产的 / 产出

senses.title: To produce a crop or result
senses.definition: to produce crops, goods, results or information
senses.definitionCN: 生产出作物、货物、结果或信息
senses.example: The field yields two harvests a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这块田一年出产两季收成。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to pay or render; land renders fruit, so the word moves from paying to producing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义是支付或交出；土地交出果实，因此这个词从「付」转向「产」。

senses.title: The amount produced
senses.definition: the quantity of a crop, product or result that is produced
senses.definitionCN: 所生产的作物、产品或结果的数量
senses.example: The wheat yield was the highest in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦产量是十年来最高的。
senses.why: The action is read as a noun: what the land hands over becomes the measurable amount.
senses.whyCN: 动作被读成名词：土地交出来的东西成了可计量的数量。

senses.title: The income from an investment
senses.definition: the income or profit an investment produces, usually as a percentage
senses.definitionCN: 投资产生的收入或利润，通常以百分比表示
senses.example: The bond yields four percent a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券每年收益百分之四。
senses.why: Capital is treated like land: it renders a return, and the rate of that return is the yield.
senses.whyCN: 资本被当作土地：它交出一份回报，而这份回报的比率就是收益率。

senses.title: To surrender or cede
senses.definition: to give up resistance or hand over control to another
senses.definitionCN: 放弃抵抗或把控制权交给对方
senses.example: The garrison yielded the city after a long siege.
senses.exampleCN: 守军在长期围困后交出了这座城市。
senses.why: The paying sense turns inward: instead of giving produce, a person gives up a position or a claim.
senses.whyCN: 「交出」义转向内部：人不再交出产物，而是交出阵地或主张。

senses.title: To give way in traffic
senses.definition: to let another vehicle or person go first
senses.definitionCN: 让另一辆车或行人先行
senses.example: Drivers must yield at the roundabout.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在环岛处必须让行。
senses.why: A small surrender becomes a rule of the road: one party gives up its priority for a moment.
senses.whyCN: 小规模的让步变成道路规则：一方暂时放弃优先通行权。

senses.title: To hand something over
senses.definition: to give possession of something to another person
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的占有权交给别人
senses.example: The tenant yielded the keys to the landlord.
senses.exampleCN: 租客把钥匙交给了房东。
senses.why: This is the plain transfer behind the abstract surrenders: an object leaves one hand for another.
senses.whyCN: 这是各种抽象让步背后的朴素转移：物件从一只手交到另一只手。

senses.title: To bend or collapse under force
senses.definition: to bend, break or give way when pressure is applied
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下弯曲、断裂或让位
senses.example: The beam yielded under the weight of the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 横梁在积雪的重压下弯了下去。
senses.why: Materials also surrender: a solid that stops resisting is said to yield, and engineers measure the point at which it does.
senses.whyCN: 材料也会屈服：停止抵抗的固体被称为屈服，工程师测量它屈服的临界点。

senses.title: To concede a point
senses.titleCN: 在争论中承认对方一点
senses.definition: to admit that an opponent's argument is valid
senses.definitionCN: 承认对方的论点有道理
senses.example: She yielded on the question of cost but not of timing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在成本问题上让了步，但在时间问题上没有。
senses.why: A person gives up ground in an argument, so yielding is a verbal form of surrendering a position.
senses.whyCN: 人在争论中放弃阵地，因此让步是交出立场在言语上的形式。

senses.title: The amount produced in a reaction
senses.definition: the amount of product obtained from a chemical reaction
senses.definitionCN: 化学反应中得到的产物数量
senses.example: The new catalyst raised the yield of the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 新催化剂提高了反应产率。
senses.why: Chemistry keeps the producing sense and measures it: the reaction hands over a quantity of product.
senses.whyCN: 化学保留了「产出」义并加以计量：反应交出一份产物数量。

intro.en: Yield goes back to an Old English verb meaning to pay or repay, and its modern senses branch from that idea of handing something over. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: yield 源自古英语表示支付或偿还的动词，现代各义都从「把东西交出去」这一想法分出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gieldan meant to pay, repay or render, especially a debt or a due.
items.cn: gieldan 意为支付、偿还或交纳，尤指债务或应缴之物。

items.en: The verb is reconstructed as *geldan 'to pay', the family that also gives German Geld 'money'; its deeper Indo-European origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 该动词被重构为「支付」的日耳曼语形式，这一族也产生德语中表示「钱」的词；它更早的印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: The form yielded meant to pay, render, give up or surrender, already wider than payment alone.
items.cn: 中古英语形式已表示支付、交出、放弃或投降，范围早就不止于付款。

items.en: Land, trees and mines came to be said to yield crops, fruit and ore, because they render what they hold.
items.cn: 土地、树木与矿藏开始被说成出产作物、果实与矿石，因为它们把所含之物交出来。

items.en: Capital was described in the same way, so the noun yield came to mean the income produced by an investment.
items.cn: 资本也以同样方式被描述，名词 yield 因此指投资所产生的收益。

items.en: Chemists count the product of a reaction as its yield, and engineers speak of a material yielding when it bends or fails.
items.cn: 化学家把反应得到的产物量称为产率，工程师则说材料在弯曲或失效时屈服。

note.en: The first group contains short words that look or sound like yield; the second group lists verbs and nouns with overlapping senses.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音与 yield 相近的短词；第二组列出意义重叠的动词与名词。

entries.definition: An area of land or a subject area; it differs in the first consonant and has no sense of producing.
entries.definitionCN: 一片土地或一个领域；首个辅音不同，没有出产的意思。

entries.definition: A protective object or to protect; it shares the long vowel but not the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 防护物或保护；共享长元音，但意义无关。

entries.definition: To hold and use a tool or power; it begins with a different consonant and means control, not production.
entries.definitionCN: 握持并使用工具或权力；首个辅音不同，意为掌控而非生产。

entries.definition: To shout loudly; it has a short vowel and no connection with crops or surrender.
entries.definitionCN: 大声喊叫；元音短促，与作物或屈服无关。

entries.definition: To make or grow something; it is the neutral word, while yield adds the image of land or capital handing something over.
entries.definitionCN: 制造或种植某物；它是中性词，而 yield 另含土地或资本交出成果的意象。

entries.definition: The amount produced by a person, machine or economy; it is the neutral noun for what yield calls a harvest or return.
entries.definitionCN: 个人、机器或经济体的产出量；它是 yield 所说收成或收益的中性对应词。

entries.definition: The total gain from an investment; yield usually measures income as a percentage, while return can include price change.
entries.definitionCN: 投资的总收益；yield 通常以百分比衡量收入，而 return 可包括价格变动。

entries.definition: To stop resisting and give control to another; it is the full action, while yield can describe a small concession.
entries.definitionCN: 停止抵抗并把控制权交给对方；它是完整动作，而 yield 可指小幅让步。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real payment root, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「支付」词根、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The root meant to pay or repay, and every sense is a form of handing something over.
normal.cn: 词根本义是支付或偿还，每个义项都是一种把东西交出去的形式。

normal.en: Land hands over fruit, capital hands over income, a garrison hands over a city.
normal.cn: 土地交出果实，资本交出收益，守军交出城市。

normal.en: Traffic rules turn surrender into a small daily courtesy: yield at the roundabout.
normal.cn: 交通规则把屈服变成日常的小礼让：在环岛让行。

normal.en: Materials yield when they stop resisting, which is why engineers measure yield strength.
normal.cn: 材料停止抵抗时就是屈服，所以工程师测量屈服强度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the finance sense: bond yield, dividend yield, high yield.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金融义：债券收益率、股息收益率、高收益。

abstract.en: Picture a tree lowering its branches under the weight of fruit, as if handing the crop down.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树在果实重量下弯下枝条，仿佛把收成递下来。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that stops pushing back and lets the pressure pass through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙不再顶回去，让压力穿过它。

abstract.en: Picture a percentage drawn as a small stream flowing out of a block of capital.
abstract.cn: 想象一个百分比画成从资本块中流出的一小股水流。

examples.en: The new variety yields more grain with less water.
examples.cn: 新品种用更少的水产出更多谷物。

examples.en: The old bridge finally yielded to the flood.
examples.cn: 那座旧桥最终在洪水中塌了。

examples.en: He refused to yield on the safety rules.
examples.cn: 他拒在安全规则上让步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一压就弯，一弯就交出」——树被果子压弯，把收成交出来 → 产出、屈服

root: 古英语 gieldan「支付、偿还、交纳」，属日耳曼语族，德语中表示「钱」的词同源；更早的印欧语来源不确定。由「交出」引申出产出、屈服、让路与收益等义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all describe something being handed over: land hands over crops, capital hands over income, an army hands over a city, a material hands over its resistance.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都描述「交出」：土地交出作物，资本交出收益，军队交出城市，材料交出抵抗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree bending under fruit, handing its crop downward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株树在果实重量下弯下，把收成递下来。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: land renders a crop, and the rendered amount becomes a measurable yield.
branches.cn: 生产：土地交出作物，交出的数量成为可计量的产量。

branches.en: CAPITAL RETURN: money is treated like land and renders an income measured as a percentage.
branches.cn: 资本回报：钱被当作土地，交出一份以百分比衡量的收入。

branches.en: GIVING GROUND: an army yields a city, a debater yields a point.
branches.cn: 让出阵地：军队交出城市，辩论者让出一个论点。

branches.en: SMALL TRANSFERS: a driver yields priority, a tenant yields keys.
branches.cn: 小规模转移：司机让出优先权，租客交出钥匙。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND CHEMICAL: a beam yields under load, a reaction yields product.
branches.cn: 材料与化学：横梁在载荷下屈服，反应产出产物。

intro.en: Yield is a native English verb that forms a small family around producing and giving way.
intro.cn: yield 是英语本族动词，围绕「出产」与「让步」形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The yield family is Germanic and has no Latin-derived relatives; Latin-based words such as produce and return belong to other families.
latinIntro.cn: yield 一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁来源的同族词；produce、return 等拉丁系词属于别的词族。

items.meaning: to pay, produce or give way

items.exampleCN: 这个农场出产两季作物。

items.example: The mine yielded silver for decades.
items.exampleCN: 这座矿出产白银数十年。

items.meaning: producing, or tending to give way
items.meaningCN: 正在出产的，或容易让步的
items.example: The yielding soil was easy to plough.
She was unyielding in the negotiation.

items.meaning: a plant or thing that produces well
items.example: This rice is a heavy yielder.

items.meaning: able to be given up or produced
items.example: The right is yieldable by agreement.
items.exampleCN: 这项权利可经协议让出。

items.meaning: producing or giving way, in compounds
items.meaningCN: 作复合词成分，表示出产或让步

items.exampleCN: 收益率曲线按期限描绘利率。

definition_zh: 返回；归还；回报；收益；退货；申报表；往返的
definition_en: to come or give back, or the gain from an investment
core_image: 一只回旋镖飞出去又回到出发点，回来时带着新的东西
scene: 新工厂投产一年后，投资人翻看账目，计算这笔投入带来的年度收益。Investors expect a steady return from the new factory.
sceneCN: 这里指「投资回报」，对应第 3 个义项：投入资金后得到的收益；句意为投资者期待新工厂带来稳定回报。画面要点：账本、工厂外景、上升的曲线。

pos.zh: 返回；归还；回报；答复；选举（某人）任职；回球
返回；归还；回报；收益；退货；申报表
往返的；回程的

senses.title: To come back to a place
senses.definition: to go or come back to a place you left
senses.definitionCN: 回到自己离开的地方
senses.example: She returned to the village after ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 她十年后回到了那个村庄。
senses.why: The core motion is a turning back: a path is followed outward and then reversed toward its start.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是折返：一条路先向外走，再朝起点反向走。

senses.title: To give something back
senses.definition: to give an object back to its owner
senses.definitionCN: 把物品还给它的主人
senses.example: Please return the book by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 请在周五前归还这本书。
senses.why: The same reversal applies to an object: it goes back to the hand it came from.
senses.whyCN: 同样的折返也用于物件：它回到原来那只手里。

senses.title: The gain from an investment
senses.definition: the profit or income produced by an investment
senses.definitionCN: 投资所产生的利润或收入
senses.example: The return on the solar plant exceeded forecasts.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳能电站的回报超过了预期。
senses.why: Money goes out and comes back larger, so the financial sense is the out-and-back path with a surplus at the end.
senses.whyCN: 资金出去又回来，而且回来时更多，因此金融义就是一条终点带有盈余的往返路径。

senses.title: To send goods back
senses.definition: to send purchased goods back to the seller
senses.definitionCN: 把买下的商品寄回卖家
senses.example: He returned the coat because the size was wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为尺码不对退回了那件外套。
senses.why: Commerce repeats the physical reversal: the goods travel back along the same route as the payment.
senses.whyCN: 商业重复了这一物理折返：货物沿着付款的同一路线返回。

senses.title: To answer or report back
senses.definition: to reply to someone or report back with information
senses.definitionCN: 回复某人或带回信息
senses.example: He promised to return with an answer by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他答应中午前带答复回来。
senses.why: Information makes the round trip: a question goes out, and the answer comes back to the asker.
senses.whyCN: 信息完成一次往返：问题出去，答案回到提问者手里。

senses.title: To come back again
senses.definition: of a feeling, season or condition, to come back after an absence
senses.definitionCN: 情感、季节或状况消失后又回来
senses.example: The pain returned in the cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷天气里疼痛又回来了。
senses.why: What leaves can come back without a traveller: a season or a feeling repeats its visit.
senses.whyCN: 离开的东西不必有旅行者也能回来：季节或情感重复它的到访。

senses.title: To elect someone to office
senses.definition: to elect a candidate to a seat in a legislature
senses.definitionCN: 把候选人选入立法机构
senses.example: The district returned a new member to parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 该选区把一位新议员送进了议会。
senses.why: An old parliamentary sense: the constituency sends a representative, who is said to be returned to the house.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个古老的议会义：选区把代表送去，代表便被称为「回到」议院。

senses.title: To hit a ball back
senses.definition: to hit a ball back to an opponent in tennis or a similar game
senses.definitionCN: 在网球等运动中把球击回对方
senses.example: She returned the serve with a fast forehand.
senses.exampleCN: 她用快速的正手回击了发球。
senses.why: The ball makes the same journey back across the net, so the word describes its return rather than the player's.
senses.whyCN: 球沿着同样的路线越过球网，因此这个词描述的是球的返回，而不是人的。

senses.title: A formal statement to authorities
senses.definition: an official form or report filed with a government or court
senses.definitionCN: 向政府或法院提交的正式表格或报告
senses.example: He filed his tax return in April.
senses.exampleCN: 他在四月提交了纳税申报表。
senses.why: A declaration travels to the authority and is kept there as a record, so the paper itself is called a return.
senses.whyCN: 申报书送到当局并被留存为记录，于是这份文书本身被称为 return。

intro.en: Return comes from a French verb meaning to turn back, built on a Latin word for turning. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: return 来自表示「转回去」的法语动词，建立在拉丁语表示「转」的词上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tornus meant a lathe, a device for turning wood, and it came into Latin from Greek tornos.
items.cn: tornus 意为旋床，是转动木材的器具，经希腊语 tornos 进入拉丁语。

items.en: Tornare meant to turn on a lathe or to round off, and its sense widened to turning in general.
items.cn: tornare 意为在旋床上转动或修圆，后来意义扩展到一般的「转」。

items.en: The prefix re- 'back' plus torner 'to turn' produced retorner, to turn back or come back.
items.cn: 前缀 re-「向后」加 torner「转」构成 retorner，意为折回或回来。

items.en: English borrowed the verb and noun, using them for coming back, giving back and reporting back.
items.cn: 英语借入动词与名词，用于回来、归还与回报。

items.en: Investors described the gain that came back from capital as the return, giving the word its financial life.
items.cn: 投资者把资本带回的增益称为 return，这赋予该词金融生命。

items.en: Parliamentary election, tennis replies and official tax statements each extended the same back-and-forth image.
items.cn: 议会选举、网球回击与正式税务申报各自延伸了同一个「往返」意象。

note.en: The first group is built on the same turning root but differs in prefix or sense; the second group contains words for coming back or for gain.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「转」的词根上，但前缀或意义不同；第二组表示「回来」或「收益」。

entries.definition: To keep or hold on to something; it uses a Latin root for holding, not turning, so it means keep rather than come back.
entries.definitionCN: 保留、握住某物；它用的是拉丁语「握持」词根而非「转」，意为保留而非回来。

entries.definition: To stop working or to withdraw; it comes from a French verb meaning to withdraw, not to turn back.
entries.definitionCN: 停止工作或退下；它出自表示「退开」的法语动词，而非「转回」。

entries.definition: To go back to a former state or owner; it is close to return but usually describes a state or right, not a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 回到以前的状态或归还原主；与 return 接近，但通常指状态或权利而非行程。

entries.definition: To rotate or change direction; it is the plain verb behind return, which adds the idea of going back.
entries.definitionCN: 旋转或改变方向；它是 return 背后的朴素动词，后者增添「回去」的意思。

entries.definition: The common phrasal verb for returning; return is the formal single-word equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 表示返回的常用短语动词；return 是正式的单字对应词。

entries.definition: To pay money back, or the money paid back; return is wider and can apply to goods or objects.
entries.definitionCN: 退还钱款，或退回的钱；return 更宽，可指货物或物品。

entries.definition: The income from an investment as a percentage; return is the total gain, including price change.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收入以百分比计；return 是总收益，包含价格变动。

entries.definition: The money left after costs; return measures gain against the amount invested, profit measures the surplus itself.
entries.definitionCN: 扣除成本后剩下的钱；return 衡量相对于投入的增益，profit 衡量盈余本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real turning root, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「转动」词根、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The word is turn plus back: a path or an object reverses direction toward its start.
normal.cn: 这个词是「转」加「回」：路径或物件反向朝起点走。

normal.en: Money that goes out and comes back larger is the financial return.
normal.cn: 出去又回来并且更多的钱，就是金融上的回报。

normal.en: A question goes out and an answer comes back, so replying is also returning.
normal.cn: 问题出去、答案回来，所以答复也是 return。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: in return, tax return, return ticket, point of no return.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示范围：作为回报、纳税申报、往返票、无法回头的临界点。

normal.en: A tax return is a paper that travels to the authority and stays there as a record.
normal.cn: 纳税申报表是一份送到当局并留存为记录的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a boomerang leaving the hand and curving back to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只回旋镖离开手，又弯回手中。

abstract.en: Picture the same loop drawn around a coin, which comes back with a smaller coin attached.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个环画在一枚硬币周围，回来时还带着一枚小硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a letter sent to an office and filed there, never travelling home again.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信送到机关并被归档，从此不再回家。

examples.en: The birds return to the same lake every spring.
examples.cn: 这些鸟每年春天回到同一片湖。

examples.en: The investment returned twelve percent in its first year.
examples.cn: 这项投资第一年回报了百分之十二。

examples.en: Please return the form to the office by Monday.
examples.cn: 请在周一前把表格交回办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「转回去」——出去的东西转回原处 → 返回、归还；钱转回来还变多 → 回报

root: 古法语 retorner「转回去」，由 re-「向后」加 torner「转」构成；后者出自拉丁语 tornare「在旋床上转动」，再上溯到希腊语表示旋床的词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all describe a round trip: a person, object, answer, season, ball, money or official paper goes out and comes back, or is sent back.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都描述一次往返：人、物件、答复、季节、球、金钱或正式文书出去又回来，或被送回。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boomerang leaving the hand and curving back to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只回旋镖离开手，又弯回手中。

branches.en: COMING BACK: a traveller or a season reverses direction and appears again.
branches.cn: 回来：旅行者或季节反向而行，再次出现。

branches.en: GIVING BACK: an object or purchased goods travel back to their owner or seller.
branches.cn: 归还：物品或买下的货物回到原主或卖家手中。

branches.en: GAIN: capital goes out and comes back with a surplus, which is the return.
branches.cn: 收益：资本出去又带着盈余回来，这就是回报。

branches.en: ANSWERS AND PAPERS: a reply, a tennis stroke and a filed form all complete a back-and-forth.
branches.cn: 答复与文书：回复、网球回击与提交表格都完成一次往返。

branches.en: ELECTION: a constituency sends a member to the house, a formal kind of return.
branches.cn: 选举：选区把议员送进议院，这是一种正式的「送回」。

intro.en: Return is a French-derived verb whose parts, a back prefix and a turning root, remain productive in English.
intro.cn: return 是法语来源的动词，其「向后」前缀与「转」词根在英语中仍有构词能力。

latinIntro.en: The turning root also gives turn, tour and tournament, all through forms of the same French verb.
latinIntro.cn: 这个「转」词根还产生 turn、tour 与 tournament，都经同一个法语动词的不同形式。

items.meaning: comes back, or gains and forms

items.example: She returned the call at once.

items.exampleCN: 返乡的工人挤满了车站。

items.example: The scheme helps returners to work.
items.exampleCN: 该计划帮助重返岗位者。

definition_en: the gain from an investment expressed as a percentage of its cost
core_image: 一只天平，一端放投入，另一端放回收，两个数字相除得出一个百分比
scene: 项目评审会上，分析师把预计收益与投入成本相除，得到一个按年计算的百分比。Analysts calculated the rate of return before approving the project.
sceneCN: 这里指「回报率」，对应第 1 个义项：收益相对于投入的百分比；句意为分析师在批准项目之前先计算了回报率。画面要点：评审桌、计算器、成本与收益两栏。

pos.zh: 回报率；收益率（常与投资、项目或资产连用）

senses.title: Gain measured against cost
senses.titleCN: 收益相对于投入的比率
senses.definition: the profit or income from an investment stated as a percentage of the amount invested
senses.definitionCN: 投资所得利润或收入占投入金额的百分比
senses.example: The project offers a rate of return of nine percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目提供百分之九的回报率。
senses.why: Rate supplies the proportion and return supplies the gain, so the phrase puts one number over another to make them comparable.
senses.whyCN: rate 提供比例，return 提供增益，这个短语把一个数放在另一个数之上，使两者可比。

senses.title: The annualized rate
senses.definition: the rate of return recalculated as if it accrued over one year
senses.definitionCN: 按一年为期限重新折算的回报率
senses.example: The fund reports an annualized rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金报告的是年化回报率。
senses.why: Periods differ, so the percentage is stretched or compressed to a one-year standard before comparisons are made.
senses.whyCN: 各期长度不同，于是百分比先被拉伸或压缩到一年的标准，再作比较。

senses.title: The minimum acceptable rate
senses.titleCN: 要求达到的最低回报率
senses.definition: the lowest return an investor or firm will accept before committing funds
senses.definitionCN: 投资者或公司在投入资金前愿意接受的最低回报
senses.example: The board set a required rate of return for new plants.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会为新工厂设定了必要回报率。
senses.why: The measure becomes a gate: capital is not released unless the projected percentage clears the threshold.
senses.whyCN: 这个指标变成一道闸门：预期百分比不过门槛，资金就不放行。

senses.title: The internal rate of return
senses.definition: the discount rate at which a project's inflows and outflows have a net present value of zero
senses.definitionCN: 使项目现金流入与流出的净现值为零的折现率
senses.example: The internal rate of return was above the cost of capital.
senses.exampleCN: 内部收益率高于资本成本。
senses.why: Here the rate is solved from the cash flows themselves rather than stated in advance, so the project's own pattern sets the number.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比率由现金流本身解出，而不是事先给定，项目的自身模式决定了这个数字。

senses.title: The real rate after inflation
senses.titleCN: 扣除通胀后的实际回报率
senses.definition: the rate of return adjusted for inflation
senses.definitionCN: 经通胀调整后的回报率
senses.example: A nominal gain can be a negative real rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 名义上的增益也可能是负的实际回报率。
senses.why: Money gains can shrink in purchasing power, so the measured percentage is corrected to show what it really buys.
senses.whyCN: 金钱上的增益可能被购买力侵蚀，因此测得的百分比要修正，以显示它真正能买到什么。

senses.title: The accounting rate of return
senses.definition: a rate calculated from accounting profit rather than cash flow
senses.definitionCN: 依据会计利润而非现金流计算的比率
senses.example: The accounting rate of return ignores the timing of cash.
senses.exampleCN: 会计收益率忽略现金的时间分布。
senses.why: Different records produce different numbers, so the phrase is qualified by the bookkeeping method that supplies the gain.
senses.whyCN: 不同的账目产生不同的数字，因此这个短语要用提供增益的记账方法来限定。

senses.title: The expected rate
senses.definition: the return an investor anticipates before the outcome is known
senses.definitionCN: 结果未知前投资者预期的回报
senses.example: Investors demand more for a risky expected rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者对高风险的预期回报要求更高。
senses.why: Before the fact the percentage is a forecast, so the phrase shifts from a realized gain to an anticipated one.
senses.whyCN: 在结果出来之前，百分比是预测，于是这个短语从已实现的增益转到预期的增益。

senses.title: The social rate of return
senses.definition: the return to society from public spending, including benefits not captured in cash
senses.definitionCN: 公共支出给社会带来的回报，包括未以现金体现的益处
senses.example: Vaccination programmes show a high social rate of return.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗接种项目显示出很高的社会回报率。
senses.why: The gain is widened from private money to public benefit, so the same ratio is applied to health, education and infrastructure.
senses.whyCN: 增益从私人金钱扩大到公共益处，同一个比率于是被用到健康、教育与基础设施上。

intro.en: Rate of return joins rate, from a Latin word for a reckoned share, with return, from a French verb for turning back. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这一短语把「比率」与「回报」两个词组合起来：前者出自拉丁语表示计算出的份额，后者出自法语表示转回去的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Reri meant to reckon, think or judge, and it built words about calculation and reason.
items.cn: reri 意为计算、思考、判断，构成了一批表示计算与理性的词。

items.en: Rata pars meant a fixed or reckoned share, and the adjective rata became the English noun rate.
items.cn: rata pars 意为确定或计算出的份额，形容词 rata 后来成为英语名词 rate。

items.en: Rate entered English as a proportion, a standard or a charge fixed by calculation.
items.cn: rate 进入英语时指比例、标准或经计算确定的收费。

items.en: Return took on the sense of the gain that comes back from capital, supplying the second half of the phrase.
items.cn: return 获得「资本带回的增益」这一意义，提供短语的后半。

items.en: Engineers and investors began to compare projects by the percentage that came back each year, fixing rate of return as a technical phrase.
items.cn: 工程师与投资者开始用每年返回的百分比比较项目，回报率这一说法于是固定为专业短语。

items.en: Modern finance multiplied its variants: internal, real, required, expected, accounting and social.
items.cn: 现代金融衍生出许多变体：内部、实际、必要、预期、会计与社会。

note.en: The first group is built from the same reckoning root; the second group contains related measures that answer different questions.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「计算」词根上；第二组是回答不同问题的相关指标。

entries.definition: A proportion or a charge per unit; alone it says nothing about gain, only about a measured relation.
entries.definitionCN: 比例或每单位的收费；单独使用时不表示增益，只表示被衡量的关系。

entries.definition: A relation between two quantities expressed as one divided by the other; a rate of return is one kind of ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 两个数量之间以一个除另一个的关系；回报率是比率的一种。

entries.definition: A fixed allowance of food or supplies; it is a reckoned share, not a financial gain.
entries.definitionCN: 食物或物资的定额；它是计算出的份额，不是金融增益。

entries.definition: Based on reason or calculation; it shares the reckoning root but describes thinking, not returns.
entries.definitionCN: 基于理性或计算的；共享「计算」词根，但描述思维而非回报。

entries.definition: The gain from an investment relative to its cost; it is the broader phrase, while rate of return often appears in project and portfolio arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 投资增益相对于成本；它是更宽的说法，而回报率常用于项目与组合计算。

entries.definition: Income from an investment as a percentage, usually ignoring price change; rate of return can include both income and capital gain.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收入以百分比计，通常忽略价格变动；回报率可同时包括收入与资本增值。

entries.definition: The percentage charged for a loan; it is the price of money, not the gain from using it.
entries.definitionCN: 贷款的收费百分比；它是资金的价格，而不是使用资金得到的增益。

entries.definition: The ability of a business to produce profit; it is a quality, while a rate of return is a number.
entries.definitionCN: 企业产生利润的能力；它是性质，而回报率是一个数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real reckoning root, the real turning root and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「计算」词根、真实的「转回」词根与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Rate means a reckoned proportion; return means gain coming back; together they put gain over cost.
normal.cn: rate 是算出的比例，return 是转回的增益；合起来就是把增益放在成本之上。

normal.en: The phrase answers one question: for every unit put in, how much comes back?
normal.cn: 这个短语回答一个问题：每投入一个单位，能回来多少？

normal.en: Annual, real, required, expected, internal and social are fixed qualifiers that change the question slightly.
normal.cn: 年度、实际、必要、预期、内部与社会这些固定限定语略微改变问题。

normal.en: Required rate is a gate; internal rate is solved from cash flows; real rate removes inflation.
normal.cn: 必要回报率是闸门；内部收益率由现金流解出；实际回报率扣除通胀。

normal.en: Rate of return is a ratio, so it is always a percentage or a decimal, never a sum of money.
normal.cn: 回报率是一个比率，所以总是百分比或小数，而不是一笔金额。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with cost on one pan and gain on the other, and a small percentage printed where the beam settles.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端放成本，另一端放增益，横梁停住处印着一个小百分比。

abstract.en: Picture the same percentage stretched over twelve months, then squeezed back for a single quarter.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个百分比被拉到十二个月，再压回一个季度。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer whose mercury is purchasing power, falling even while the money number rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一支温度计里的水银是购买力，金钱数字上升时它却在下降。

examples.en: The plant achieved a rate of return above the industry average.
examples.cn: 这家工厂的回报率高于行业平均。

examples.en: A negative real rate of return erodes savings silently.
examples.cn: 负的实际回报率在不知不觉中侵蚀储蓄。

examples.en: They rejected the plan because its internal rate of return was too low.
examples.cn: 他们否决了该计划，因为其内部收益率太低。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「回来的比例」——投入一笔钱，看返回来的部分占多少 → 回报率

root: rate 出自拉丁语 rata pars「计算出的份额」，源于 reri「计算、判断」；return 出自法语表示「转回去」的动词。两者合指收益相对于投入的比率。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all express one ratio, then qualify it by time, by threshold, by method, by inflation, by expectation and by who receives the benefit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表达同一个比率，再按时间、门槛、方法、通胀、预期与受益者加以限定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with cost on one pan and gain on the other, printing a percentage.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一端放成本，另一端放增益，并印出一个百分比。

branches.en: BASE RATIO: gain divided by cost gives the plain measure.
branches.cn: 基础比率：增益除以成本，得到最朴素的指标。

branches.en: TIME AND EXPECTATION: the same ratio is annualized, or projected before the outcome is known.
branches.cn: 时间与预期：同一比率被年化，或在结果未知前被预测。

branches.en: THRESHOLD: the ratio becomes a minimum that capital must clear.
branches.cn: 门槛：这个比率成为资金必须越过的下限。

branches.en: METHOD: cash flows solve an internal rate, while accounting profit produces a book rate.
branches.cn: 方法：现金流解出内部收益率，会计利润产生账面收益率。

branches.en: REAL AND SOCIAL: inflation is removed, or private gain is widened to public benefit.
branches.cn: 实际与社会：或扣除通胀，或把私人增益扩大到公共益处。

intro.en: Rate of return is a phrase made of two Latin-derived words, and each brings a family of related terms.
intro.cn: 这一短语由两个拉丁来源词构成，各自带来一族相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin reri 'to reckon' gives rate, ratio, ration, rational and reason; return comes through French from a Latin turning word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reri「计算」衍生 rate、ratio、ration、rational 与 reason；return 经法语出自拉丁语表示「转」的词。

The ratio of debt to income matters.
items.exampleCN: 债务与收入的比率很重要。

able to be assessed or taxed

definition_zh: 风险；危险；冒险；风险源；保险风险
definition_en: the possibility of loss or harm, or to put something in danger
core_image: 一个人站在悬崖边，手里握着绳子，另一端系着货物
scene: 银行信贷员在签下大额贷款前，反复核对借款人的还款能力与抵押物价值。Every lender must weigh the risk before signing a loan.
sceneCN: 这里指「损失的可能性」，对应第 1 个义项：可能发生的不利结果；句意为每位放贷者在签贷款前都必须权衡风险。画面要点：贷款合同、抵押物照片、风险评估表。

pos.zh: 风险；危险；风险源；（保险）风险对象
使……冒风险；冒险做

senses.title: Possibility of loss or harm
senses.definition: the chance that something bad may happen
senses.definitionCN: 坏事可能发生的概率
senses.example: There is a risk of flooding in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里有发生洪水的风险。
senses.why: The core sense is uncertainty turned toward harm: not every unknown is a risk, only one that may cost something.
senses.whyCN: 核心意义是朝向伤害的不确定性：不是所有未知都是风险，只有可能造成损失的那一种才算。

senses.title: A specific hazard or threat
senses.definition: a person, thing or situation that may cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的人、物或情形
senses.example: Faulty wiring is a serious fire risk.
senses.exampleCN: 布线故障是严重的火灾隐患。
senses.why: The abstract chance is attached to a concrete source, so the word can name the thing that carries the danger.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的概率被附着到具体来源上，于是这个词可以指承载危险的那个东西。

senses.title: Financial exposure
senses.definition: the amount of money that could be lost in a transaction or investment
senses.definitionCN: 在一笔交易或投资中可能损失的金额
senses.example: The bank reduced its risk in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该银行减少了在该地区的风险敞口。
senses.why: In finance the possible harm is measured in money, so risk becomes the size of the position that could be lost.
senses.whyCN: 在金融中，可能的伤害以金钱计量，于是风险变成可能损失的持仓规模。

senses.title: To put something in danger
senses.definition: to expose something valuable to possible loss
senses.definitionCN: 使有价值之物面临可能的损失
senses.example: He risked his savings on the new business.
senses.exampleCN: 他把积蓄押在这门新生意上。
senses.why: As a verb the chance becomes an act: the person places a valued thing where harm can reach it.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，概率变成动作：人把珍视之物放到伤害能够触及的地方。

senses.title: To take a chance of doing something
senses.definition: to do something that may bring a bad result
senses.definitionCN: 做可能带来坏结果的事
senses.example: She risked losing her job by speaking out.
senses.exampleCN: 她冒着丢工作的风险发声。
senses.why: The verb extends from things to actions: the act itself is placed in the path of possible harm.
senses.whyCN: 动词从东西扩展到行为：行为本身被放到可能受害的路径上。

senses.title: An insured person or property
senses.definition: a person or property insured against loss, as seen by an insurer
senses.definitionCN: 保险公司承保的人或财产
senses.example: The insurer refused to cover such a high risk.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司拒绝承保这样高风险的对象。
senses.why: Insurance reverses the viewpoint: what the insured calls a danger, the insurer calls the risk it holds on its books.
senses.whyCN: 保险颠倒视角：投保人称为危险的东西，保险公司称为账上的风险对象。

senses.title: A borrower likely to default
senses.definition: a borrower or counterparty whose failure is likely
senses.definitionCN: 很可能无法履约的借款方或交易对手
senses.example: The loan book is full of poor risks.
senses.exampleCN: 这本贷款账上满是劣质客户。
senses.why: Lending turns a probability into a label for a person, so a bad borrower is called a risk by metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 放贷把概率变成对人的标签，于是不良借款人被借代称为一个风险。

senses.title: Measurable volatility
senses.definition: the statistical variability of returns, used to price uncertain outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 收益的统计波动性，用于为不确定结果定价
senses.example: The model assigns a risk to each asset.
senses.exampleCN: 模型为每项资产指定一个风险值。
senses.why: Modern finance replaces vague danger with a number, so risk becomes a measured spread of possible returns.
senses.whyCN: 现代金融用数字取代模糊的危险，于是风险成了可能回报的受测分布。

intro.en: Risk entered English from French and Italian, and the deeper origin of the word is disputed rather than settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: risk 从法语与意大利语进入英语，这个词更深的来源仍有争议，并非定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sixteenth-century French risque meant danger or a hazard, especially at sea.
items.cn: 十六世纪法语 risque 意为危险或风险，尤指海上的风险。

items.en: The French form is generally thought to come from Italian risco or rischio, a danger run into by a ship or cargo.
items.cn: 法语形式一般被认为出自意大利语 risco 或 rischio，指船只或货物遭遇的危险。

items.en: Two explanations compete: one connects it with Greek rhiza 'root', imagined as a reef a ship strikes, and another with Latin resecare 'to cut off'. Neither is proven, so the deeper source remains source uncertain.
items.cn: 有两种竞争性解释：一种把它与希腊语表示「根」的词联系起来，想象为船撞上的暗礁；另一种与拉丁语表示「切掉」的词联系起来。两者都未被证明，因此更深来源仍属来源不确定。

items.en: English adopted risk for the chance of loss in trade and at sea, and the verb followed the noun.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用于贸易与海上的损失可能，动词随后也由名词派生出来。

items.en: Marine insurers spoke of the risks they carried, which produced the sense of an insured person or ship as a risk.
items.cn: 海上保险人谈论自己所承担的风险，由此产生「被承保的人或船就是一项风险」的用法。

items.en: Statistical finance turned risk into a measurable dispersion of returns and a number attached to positions.
items.cn: 统计金融把风险变成可计量的收益离散度，以及附着在持仓上的一个数字。

note.en: The first group contains short words that look or sound like risk; the second group lists words for danger and for uncertainty.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音与 risk 相近的短词；第二组是表示危险与不确定的词。

entries.definition: To go upward; it ends in a voiced consonant and has no connection with danger.
entries.definitionCN: 上升；以浊辅音结尾，与危险无关。

entries.definition: A skating area; the final sound is different and the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 滑冰场；结尾音不同，意义无关。

entries.definition: A stack of hay or straw; it is a noun for a farm object, not a chance of loss.
entries.definitionCN: 草堆；它是农用物件的名词，不是损失的概率。

entries.definition: Quick and energetic; it adds an initial consonant and describes speed, not danger.
entries.definitionCN: 轻快而有活力的；多了一个开头辅音，描述速度而非危险。

entries.definition: A situation in which harm is likely now; danger is more immediate, while risk is the chance of harm ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 眼下很可能造成伤害的处境；danger 更即时，risk 是未来受害的概率。

entries.definition: A specific source of danger, such as ice on a road; hazard is the thing, risk is the chance it causes loss.
entries.definitionCN: 具体的危险来源，如路面结冰；hazard 是那个东西，risk 是它造成损失的概率。

entries.definition: The amount by which one is affected by a factor; in finance it is the size of the position at risk.
entries.definitionCN: 受某因素影响的程度；在金融中即处于风险中的持仓规模。

entries.definition: The state of not knowing what will happen; uncertainty may be good or bad, while risk points toward loss.
entries.definitionCN: 不知道会发生什么的状态；不确定性可好可坏，而风险指向损失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real maritime origin, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的海上来源、真实复合词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The word came through French and Italian trade language for dangers at sea.
normal.cn: 这个词经法语与意大利语的贸易语言而来，原指海上的危险。

normal.en: Risk is not every unknown; it is uncertainty that can cost you something.
normal.cn: 风险不是所有未知，而是可能让你付出代价的不确定。

normal.en: Finance measures risk as the size of a position that could be lost.
normal.cn: 金融把风险衡量为可能损失的持仓规模。

normal.en: Insurance calls the insured ship or person a risk, which shows how the viewpoint flips.
normal.cn: 保险把被承保的船或人称为一项风险，显示了视角如何翻转。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: take a risk, at risk, credit risk, risk management.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示范围：冒险、处于危险中、信用风险、风险管理。

abstract.en: Picture a person at the edge of a cliff holding a rope tied to valuable cargo.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在悬崖边，手里握着系有贵重货物的绳子。

abstract.en: Picture the same cliff edge redrawn as a number on a screen, still measuring what could fall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个悬崖边缘被改画成屏幕上的数字，仍在衡量可能掉落的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a ship approaching a hidden reef, the old picture behind the modern word.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船驶向隐藏的暗礁，这是现代词背后的古老画面。

examples.en: Smoking raises the risk of heart disease.
examples.cn: 吸烟提高心脏病的风险。

examples.en: The company took a risk by entering the new market.
examples.cn: 公司进入新市场是冒了风险。

examples.en: Investors are paid more for bearing more risk.
examples.cn: 投资者承担更多风险，就获得更多回报。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「悬崖边的绳子」——可能掉下去，也可能拉住 → 风险

root: 经法语 risque 与意大利语 risco 进入英语，原指海上遭遇的危险；更早来源有「暗礁」与「切掉」两种竞争性解释，均未证实，属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain chance of harm to a concrete hazard, then to money at stake, to the act of risking, to insurance labels and finally to measured volatility.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般的受害概率，转到具体危险源，再到押上的金钱、冒险动作、保险标签，最后到可计量的波动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a cliff edge holding a rope tied to valuable cargo.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在悬崖边，手里握着系有贵重货物的绳子。

branches.en: BASE CHANCE: uncertainty is read only where loss is possible.
branches.cn: 基础概率：只有当损失可能发生时，不确定性才被读成风险。

branches.en: SOURCE AND ACTION: a faulty wire is a risk, and speaking out risks a job.
branches.cn: 来源与动作：故障电线是风险，公开发声则拿工作冒险。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: finance turns the chance into the size of a position and the spread of returns.
branches.cn: 计量：金融把概率变成持仓规模与收益离散度。

branches.en: EXPOSING: the verb places something valued where harm can reach it.
branches.cn: 暴露：动词把珍视之物放到伤害能够触及之处。

branches.en: INSURANCE AND LENDING: the insurer or lender labels the person or property as the risk itself.
branches.cn: 保险与放贷：保险人或放贷者把人或财产直接标为风险。

intro.en: Risk is a borrowed Romance word that compounds freely in finance, insurance and everyday speech.
intro.cn: risk 是借入的罗曼语词，在金融、保险与日常语言中能自由复合。

latinIntro.en: There is no secure Latin root behind risk, so no Latin-derived family is listed; the word's deeper etymology is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: risk 背后没有可靠的拉丁词根，因此不列拉丁同族词；这个词更深的词源仍有争议。

items.example: Government bills are treated as risk-free.

不愿冒险的储蓄者偏好存款。

definition_en: the risk of losing money through financial transactions, markets or obligations
core_image: 一张资产负债表上有一处正在渗水的裂缝
scene: 货币危机之后，银行重新审查资产负债表，评估汇率波动与坏账可能带来的损失。The bank reviewed its financial risk after the currency crisis.
sceneCN: 这里指「金融风险」，对应第 1 个义项：因金融交易、市场或债务而蒙受损失的可能；句意为货币危机之后，银行重新审查了自身金融风险。画面要点：资产负债表、汇率曲线、风险审查章。

pos.zh: 财务风险；金融风险（可数指具体一类风险）

senses.title: Exposure to monetary loss
senses.titleCN: 蒙受金钱损失的可能性
senses.definition: the possibility of losing money through financial activities
senses.definitionCN: 因金融活动而损失金钱的可能性
senses.example: The audit found serious financial risk in the subsidiary.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现该子公司存在严重的金融风险。
senses.why: Financial narrows risk to money, so the broad chance of harm becomes a chance of loss measured in currency.
senses.whyCN: financial 把风险收窄到金钱，于是广义的受害概率变成以货币计量的损失概率。

senses.title: Credit risk
senses.definition: the risk that a borrower or counterparty fails to pay
senses.definitionCN: 借款人或交易对手无法付款的风险
senses.example: Credit risk rose as small firms struggled.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业陷入困境，信用风险随之上升。
senses.why: One source of loss is another party's failure, so the general exposure is narrowed to who owes the money.
senses.whyCN: 损失的一个来源是对方违约，于是普遍敞口被收窄到「谁欠着钱」。

senses.title: Market risk
senses.definition: the risk that prices, rates or indices move against a position
senses.definitionCN: 价格、利率或指数朝持仓不利方向变动的风险
senses.example: Market risk dominates a trading book.
senses.exampleCN: 市场风险在交易账簿中占主导。
senses.why: Another source is the market itself, where prices move without anyone defaulting.
senses.whyCN: 另一个来源是市场本身：价格会变动，却没有任何人违约。

senses.title: Liquidity risk
senses.definition: the risk of being unable to meet obligations when they fall due
senses.definitionCN: 到期无法履行义务的风险
senses.example: Liquidity risk can sink a solvent bank.
senses.exampleCN: 流动性风险能拖垮一家仍有偿付能力的银行。
senses.why: The danger is not lack of assets but lack of ready cash, so the word focuses on timing rather than value.
senses.whyCN: 危险不是没有资产，而是没有随时可用的现金，所以这个词聚焦于时点而非价值。

senses.title: Operational risk
senses.definition: the risk of loss from failed processes, people, systems or fraud
senses.definitionCN: 流程、人员、系统失败或欺诈造成损失的风险
senses.example: Operational risk includes errors and internal theft.
senses.exampleCN: 操作风险包括差错与内部盗窃。
senses.why: The source moves inside the firm: the machinery and people meant to handle money can themselves fail.
senses.whyCN: 来源移到公司内部：本应处理金钱的机械与人员本身也会失灵。

senses.title: Currency risk
senses.definition: the risk that exchange rates change the value of foreign payments or assets
senses.definitionCN: 汇率变动改变外币付款或资产价值的风险
senses.example: Exporters face currency risk on every contract.
senses.exampleCN: 出口商在每份合同上都面临汇率风险。
senses.why: When money itself changes price across borders, even a safe asset can lose value at home.
senses.whyCN: 当货币本身在跨境之间改变价格，连安全的资产也可能在本国贬值。

senses.title: Systemic risk
senses.definition: the risk that one failure spreads through the whole financial system
senses.definitionCN: 单一失败蔓延至整个金融体系的风险
senses.example: Regulators watch systemic risk across banks.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者监测跨银行的系统性风险。
senses.why: The unit of danger grows from a firm to the system, so a local loss becomes a threat to everyone.
senses.whyCN: 危险的单位从一家机构扩大到整个体系，局部的损失于是成为对所有人的威胁。

senses.title: Risk to capital and earnings
senses.definition: the risk that a firm's capital or earnings fall below what is required
senses.definitionCN: 公司资本或盈利跌破要求水平的风险
senses.example: The quarterly report modelled financial risk against capital.
senses.exampleCN: 季度报告以资本为基准对金融风险作了建模。
senses.why: Risk management compares possible losses with the buffer available, so the exposure is read as a threat to solvency.
senses.whyCN: 风险管理把可能损失与可用缓冲相比较，于是敞口被读成对偿付能力的威胁。

intro.en: Financial risk joins financial, from a French word for settling a debt, with risk, a Romance loan whose deeper origin is disputed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: financial risk 把 financial 与 risk 组合起来：前者出自法语表示结清债务的词，后者是来源有争议的罗曼语借词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Finis meant an end or boundary, and it built words about ending, limiting and settling.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界，构成了一批表示结束、限定与结清的词。

items.en: Finer meant to settle a debt or bring a matter to an end, from the same notion of a boundary being closed.
items.cn: finer 意为结清债务或把事办完，来自同一个「划上边界」的观念。

items.en: Finance named the payment or settlement of a debt, and English borrowed it for money management in general.
items.cn: finance 指债务的支付或结清，英语借来表示一般意义上的资金管理。

items.en: The adjective financial was formed to describe matters of money, revenue and funding.
items.cn: 形容词 financial 用来描述金钱、收入与筹资事务。

items.en: Risk came through French and Italian; its deeper origin is source uncertain, with a Greek reef explanation and a Latin cutting explanation both unproven.
items.cn: risk 经法语与意大利语而来；更深来源不确定，暗礁说与切掉说都未获证明。

items.en: Twentieth-century regulation split financial risk into credit, market, liquidity, operational, currency and systemic types.
items.cn: 二十世纪监管把金融风险分成信用、市场、流动性、操作、汇率与系统性等类型。

note.en: The first group is built from the same finance root and is easily confused; the second group names particular risks or wider dangers.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「财务」词根上，容易混淆；第二组指具体风险或更广的危险。

entries.definition: The management of money, or to provide funds; it is the field, not the danger within it.
entries.definitionCN: 资金管理，或提供资金；它是领域，而不是领域内的危险。

entries.definition: Relating to money; it describes the kind of risk but does not by itself mean risk.
entries.definitionCN: 与金钱有关的；它描述风险的种类，本身并不表示风险。

entries.definition: A person who deals in large sums or arranges funding; it is a role, not a danger.
entries.definitionCN: 处理大额资金或安排融资的人；它是角色，不是危险。

entries.definition: A sum paid as a penalty, or excellent; the penalty sense comes from the idea of settling a matter, not from finance itself.
entries.definitionCN: 罚款，或优秀的；罚款义出自「把事结清」的观念，而非金融本身。

entries.definition: The risk that a borrower defaults; it is one component of financial risk, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 借款人违约的风险；它是金融风险的一个组成部分，而非整个类别。

entries.definition: The risk of loss from price movements; like credit risk, it is a part of the wider financial category.
entries.definitionCN: 价格变动造成损失的风险；与信用风险一样，是更广类别的一部分。

entries.definition: The size of a position affected by a factor; financial risk is the possibility, exposure is the measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 受某因素影响的持仓规模；金融风险是可能性，敞口是被计量的数额。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to pay debts; it is a result that financial risk may produce, not the risk itself.
entries.definitionCN: 无力偿还债务的状态；它是金融风险可能导致的结果，而非风险本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real settling root of finance, the disputed origin of risk, and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「结清」词根、来源有争议的 risk，以及真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Finance began as settling a debt; adding risk turns settlement into possible loss.
normal.cn: finance 最初指结清债务；加上 risk，结清就变成可能的损失。

normal.en: The phrase covers subtypes: credit, market, liquidity, operational, currency and systemic.
normal.cn: 这个短语涵盖多个子类：信用、市场、流动性、操作、汇率与系统性。

normal.en: Credit risk asks who may not pay; market risk asks what prices may do; liquidity risk asks when cash may fail.
normal.cn: 信用风险问谁可能不付钱；市场风险问价格可能怎么走；流动性风险问现金何时会断。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: financial risk management, exposure, systemic financial risk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：金融风险管理、风险敞口、系统性金融风险。

normal.en: Operational risk comes from inside, while systemic risk grows until it reaches everyone.
normal.cn: 操作风险来自内部，系统性风险则扩大到波及所有人。

abstract.en: Picture a balance sheet with one seam leaking, and no one yet knows how far the leak will spread.
abstract.cn: 想象一张资产负债表上有一道缝在渗水，还没人知道会渗多远。

abstract.en: Picture six pipes feeding one tank, each with its own valve that could fail.
abstract.cn: 想象六条管道通向同一只水箱，每条都有自己的阀门可能失灵。

abstract.en: Picture a single bank's stumble drawn as a crack running through a whole wall of banks.
abstract.cn: 想象一家银行的失足被画成一道裂纹，贯穿整面由银行砌成的墙。

examples.en: The treasurer monitors financial risk every week.
examples.cn: 财务主管每周监测金融风险。

examples.en: Diversification lowers financial risk without removing it.
examples.cn: 分散化降低金融风险，但不能消除它。

examples.en: A sudden currency fall can turn a safe loan into financial risk.
examples.cn: 货币骤然下跌能把一笔安全贷款变成金融风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「金钱上的裂缝」——账面上有一处可能漏水 → 金融风险

root: financial 出自法语 finance「债务的结清、支付」，再上溯到拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」；risk 经法语与意大利语而来，更早来源不确定。两者合指因金融活动蒙受损失的可能。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the general chance of monetary loss and then divide it by source: borrower, market, timing, operations, currency and the whole system, ending with capital adequacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般的金钱损失概率开始，再按来源划分：借款方、市场、时点、操作、货币与整个体系，最后落在资本充足性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance sheet with one seam leaking, and no one knows how far the leak will spread.
core.cn: 核心意象：资产负债表上有一道缝在渗水，没人知道会渗多远。

branches.en: THE WHOLE EXPOSURE: every financial activity carries a chance of monetary loss.
branches.cn: 整体敞口：每一项金融活动都带有金钱损失的可能。

branches.en: CREDIT: the borrower or counterparty may fail to pay.
branches.cn: 信用：借款人或交易对手可能不付钱。

branches.en: MARKET AND CAPITAL: prices move against positions, and losses eat into the capital buffer.
branches.cn: 市场与资本：价格朝持仓不利方向走，损失侵蚀资本缓冲。

branches.en: LIQUIDITY: the money exists but not at the moment it is due.
branches.cn: 流动性：钱存在，却不在到期的那一刻可用。

branches.en: OPERATIONS, CURRENCY AND SYSTEM: internal failure, exchange-rate shifts and contagion each add a source.
branches.cn: 操作、货币与体系：内部失灵、汇率变动与传染各自增添一个来源。

intro.en: Financial risk joins a Latin-derived adjective about settling accounts with a Romance noun for danger.
intro.cn: financial risk 把表示结清账目的拉丁来源形容词，与表示危险的罗曼语名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis 'end, boundary' gives finance, final, finish and infinite; the first element of this phrase belongs to that family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」衍生 finance、final、finish 与 infinite；这个短语的前半属于该词族。

这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

items.exampleCN: 一位金融家资助了这条铁路。

items.meaning: to replace a loan with a new one

items.exampleCN: 报告列出五种金融风险。
